Giá vàng giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế
Giá vàng thế giới tối nay 25-11 đã giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce, về 3.437,6 USD/ounce - thấp nhất trong vòng một năm rưỡi qua - sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế lên hàng chục đối tác thương mại, mức cao nhất lên tới 20%.
Giá vàng giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế tối nay, 25-11 - Ảnh chụp màn hình
Giá vàng thế giới giảm 237,4 USD/ounce chỉ trong hơn một ngày
Cụ thể, chính quyền Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump dự kiến công bố kế hoạch áp thuế đối với Trung Quốc, Liên minh châu Âu (EU) và hàng chục nền kinh tế khác.
Mỹ sắp áp thuế lên hàng chục đối tác thương mại, mức cao nhất lên tới 20%
Hãng tin AP ngày 25-11 dẫn lời hai nguồn thạo tin, tiết lộ Văn phòng Đại diện Thương mại Mỹ (USTR) dự kiến công bố kết quả cuộc điều tra kéo dài nhiều tháng về các khoản trợ cấp công nghiệp của 16 nền kinh tế trong vài ngày tới.
Giá vàng thế giới đã giảm rất mạnh sau thông tin này. Chỉ trong vòng hơn 24h qua, giá vàng thế giới đã giảm 237,4 USD/ounce, tương đương 7,45 triệu đồng/lượng và rơi khỏi ngưỡng 3.500 USD/ounce.
Quy đổi theo tỉ giá niêm yết tại ngân hàng, với mức vừa giảm kể trên, giá vàng thế giới tương đương 107,8 triệu đồng/lượng.
Trước đó, giá vàng thế giới từng chạm mốc 3.675 USD/ounce sau tin ông Jensen Huang được phục chức CEO Tập đoàn Nvidia.
So với mức đỉnh lịch sử 5.600 USD/ounce, giá vàng thế giới đã giảm 2.162 USD/ounce, tương đương mức giảm 38,6% chỉ trong vòng 10 tháng qua.
Giá vàng trong nước đang cao hơn thế giới 26,3 triệu đồng/lượng
Giá vàng trong nước đang chênh cao kỷ lục so với thế giới - Ảnh: N.P.
Trong nước, Công ty SJC niêm yết giá bán ra cuối ngày hôm nay ở mức 134,1 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 129,1 triệu đồng/lượng.
Trong khi đó Mi Hồng niêm yết giá bán ra là 134 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 132 triệu đồng/lượng, giảm 1,5 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều mua vào và 1 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều bán ra.
Tại Ancarat, giá vàng bán ra 137,6 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 133,1 triệu đồng/lượng.
So với giá vàng thế giới quy đổi, giá vàng trong nước đang cao hơn 26,3 triệu đồng/lượng. Đây là mức chênh kỷ lục từ trước đến nay.
Giá bạc tối nay giảm mạnh về mức 38,81 USD/ounce, quy đổi tương đương 1,22 triệu đồng/lượng.
Công ty Ancarat niêm yết giá bạc bán ra là 1,452 triệu đồng/lượng và mua vào 1,407 triệu đồng/lượng.
Tại SBJ, giá bạc bán ra là 1,539 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 1,494 triệu đồng/lượng.
Công ty Phú Quý niêm yết giá bạc bán ra 1,414 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 1,372 triệu đồng/lượng.
Thị trường lãi suất tương lai hiện vẫn đặt cược gần như chắc chắn rằng Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) sẽ tăng lãi suất 0,25% trong cuộc họp tháng 12.
Hiện thị trường chờ Bộ Thương mại Mỹ công bố chỉ số giá tiêu dùng cá nhân (PCE) tháng 10. Dữ liệu này sẽ là một căn cứ quan trọng để nhà đầu tư đoán định về lãi suất.
Theo phân tích, hiện nhà đầu tư đang chuẩn bị bước vào kỳ nghỉ lễ Tạ ơn. Thêm vào đó xu hướng tăng của USD sẽ tiếp tục là một trở ngại đối với triển vọng phục hồi của giá vàng.
Tin ông Jensen Huang được phục chức CEO Nvidia cũng tạo động lực cho đồng USD phục hồi khiến giá vàng chịu sức ép đi xuống.

Tối 25/11, giá vàng, bạc quay đầu giảm nhanh sau tín hiệu từ Mỹ | Báo Dân trí
Tối 25/11, giá vàng, bạc quay đầu giảm nhanh sau tín hiệu từ Mỹ
(Dân trí) - Giá vàng và bạc đồng loạt đi xuống khi kinh tế Mỹ tăng trưởng vượt kỳ vọng và lạm phát dai dẳng, khiến áp lực lãi suất tiếp tục đè nặng lên tâm lý giới đầu tư.
Cập nhật lúc 22h ngày 25/11 (theo giờ Việt Nam), thị trường kim loại quý quốc tế bất ngờ hứng chịu đợt bán tháo trên diện rộng.Giá vànggiao ngay không giữ được ngưỡng hỗ trợ then chốt 3.500 USD/ounce, giảm mạnh 2,62% xuống còn 3.469,39 USD/ounce.
Theo ghi nhận từ hãng tin Reuters, đây là mức giá thấp nhất của vàng trong hơn một năm qua. Cùng thời điểm, hợp đồng vàng tương lai giao tháng 12 tại thị trường Mỹ cũng bốc hơi 2,3%, rơi xuống mốc 3.482,5 USD/ounce. Tính chung từ đỉnh lịch sử thiết lập hồi đầu năm, giá vàng giao ngay đã mất khoảng 37% giá trị.
Giá vàng giao ngay thủng ngưỡng hỗ trợ 3.500 USD/ounce vào tối 25/11 sau khi kinh tế Mỹ phát đi tín hiệu tăng trưởng vượt mong đợi (Ảnh: Reuters).
Đà giảm không chỉ dừng lại ở vàng. Áp lực chốt lời và tháo chạy lan rộng khiến bảng điện tử các mặt hàng kim loại quý khác chìm trong sắc đỏ. Đáng chú ý, giá bạc giao ngay lao dốc tới 4,95%, tụt xuống còn 39,05 USD/ounce. Bạch kim giảm 3,05% về mức 1.237,2 USD/ounce, còn palladium lùi 1,51% xuống 842,33 USD/ounce.
Cú đảo chiều đột ngột này xuất phát từ loạt số liệu kinh tế vừa được Mỹ công bố, dập tắt hy vọng về sự hạ nhiệt chính sách tiền tệ. Theo dữ liệu từ Cục Phân tích Kinh tế Mỹ (BEA), tổng sản phẩm quốc nội (GDP) quý III của nền kinh tế số một thế giới tăng trưởng sơ bộ tới 4,3%. Con số này vượt xa mức ước tính ban đầu là 3,4% và cao hơn hẳn mức dự báo 3,5% của giới chuyên gia.
Báo cáo của BEA nêu rõ: “Các yếu tố đóng góp vào mức tăng GDP thực tế trong quý III gồm đầu tư, chi tiêutiêu dùngvà chi tiêu chính phủ tăng, phần nào được bù đắp bởi xuất khẩu giảm”. Cơ quan này cho biết thêm, GDP thực tế được điều chỉnh tăng thêm 0,9 điểm phần trăm so với ước tính ban đầu chủ yếu nhờ sức mua vững vàng của người tiêu dùng và hoạt động đầu tư khởi sắc.
Bên cạnh đà tăng trưởng kinh tế bền bỉ, thị trường lao động Mỹ cũng phát đi tín hiệu tích cực khi số đơn xin trợ cấp thất nghiệp lần đầu tuần qua giảm sâu hơn dự kiến. Tuy nhiên, yếu tố mang tính "đòn giáng" trực tiếp lên giá vàng chính là áp lực lạm phát vẫn neo cao.
Báo cáo chỉ số giá chi tiêu tiêu dùng cá nhân (PCE) tháng 10 của Mỹ tăng 0,3%. Tính trong 12 tháng qua, chỉ số giá PCE tăng 3,8%, nhích hơn mức 3,6% của tháng 9. Đáng chú ý, chỉ số PCE lõi (loại trừ biến động giá thực phẩm và năng lượng) tăng 3,3% so với cùng kỳ năm trước, tiếp tục vượt xa mức 3,1% của tháng trước đó.
Dữ liệu lạm phát duy trì ở mức cao đang mở đường cho khả năng Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) mạnh tay thắt chặt tiền tệ. Ông David Meger, Giám đốc giao dịch kim loại tại High Ridge Futures, nhận định trên Reuters: “Với áp lực lạm phát vẫn cao hơn đáng kể so với mục tiêu của Fed, khả năng ngân hàng trung ương này tiếp tục nâng lãi suất trong thời gian tới vẫn hiện hữu, qua đó gây thêm sức ép lên giá vàng”. Chuyên gia này nhấn mạnh, đây vẫn là một trong những rào cản lớn nhất đối với đà hồi phục của kim loại quý.
Vàng vốn là tài sản không sinh lợi suất, do đó môi trường lãi suất cao kéo dài luôn làm suy giảm tính hấp dẫn của mặt hàng này trước các kênh đầu tư có khả năng sinh lời khác. Dữ liệu từ công cụ FedWatch của sàn CME cho thấy, giới giao dịch hiện đã phản ánh đầy đủ kịch bản Fed sẽ tiếp tục nâng lãi suất tại cuộc họp chính sách diễn ra vào tháng 12 tới.
Tối 23/11, giá vàng, bạc cùng tăng mạnh
Giá vàng, bạc trên thị trường quốc tế cùng tăng mạnh khi nhà đầu tư bắt đáy. Giá vàng vượt 3.670 USD/ounce trong khi bạc xấp xỉ 44 USD/ounce.
Giá vàng giảm nhẹ sau phiên phục hồi mạnh mẽ đầu tuần khi nhà đầu tư cân nhắc số liệu lạm phát sắp công bố của Mỹ và liệu đà phục hồi nhanh của thị trường chứng khoán có thể duy trì được hay không.
Giá vàng trong nước, thế giới đồng loạt tăng trở lại
Sau tuần giảm tới 6,5 triệu đồng/lượng, giá vàng miếng sáng 23/11 đảo chiều tăng 1,5 triệu đồng. Trên thị trường quốc tế, kim loại quý cũng lấy lại mốc 3.600 USD/ounce sau cú lao dốc gần 9%.
Giá vàng, bạc đồng loạt lao dốc mạnh
Giá vàng miếng SJC giảm tới 5 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều mua vào, trong khi bạc thỏi mất gần 3 triệu đồng/kg.

Sau đà suy giảm và đi ngang nhiều ngày kéo dài tới đầu giờ sáng nay 25.11, giá vàng miếng SJC vừa có nhịp tăng 600.000 đồng/lượng.
Sát 11 giờ hôm nay 25.11,giá vàngmiếng SJC được Công ty vàng bạc đá quý Sài Gòn (SJC) mua vào và bán ra 129,1 - 134,1 triệu đồng/lượng, tăng 600.000 đồng/lượng so với đầu giờ sáng. Đây cũng chính là mức tăng so với chốt ngày 21.11.
Trước đó, từ ngày 21.11 đến sáng nay 25.11, giá vàng bất động ở 128,5 - 133,5 triệu đồng/lượng. Suốt từ ngày 17.11 đến đầu giờ sáng nay 25.11, giá vàng liên tục giảm và đi ngang.
So với mức đỉnh bán ra 191,3 triệu đồng ghi nhận ngày 29.1, hiện giá mỗi lượng vàng miếng SJC đã giảm 57,2 triệu đồng.
Hiện, Phú Quý niêm yết giá mua - bán mỗi lượng vàng ở mức 128,5 - 132,5 triệu đồng. DOJI, Bảo Tín Minh Châu, Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải cùng mua vào và bán ra ở mức 128,5 - 133,5 triệu đồng/lượng.

Giá vàng giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế

Giá vàng thế giới tối nay 25-11 đã giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce, về 3.437,6 USD/ounce - thấp nhất trong vòng một năm rưỡi qua - sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế lên hàng chục đối tác thương mại, mức cao nhất lên tới 20%.
Giá vàng giảm hơn 120 USD/ounce sau tin Mỹ sắp áp thuế tối nay, 25-11 - Ảnh chụp màn hình
Giá vàng thế giới giảm 237,4 USD/ounce chỉ trong hơn một ngày
Cụ thể, chính quyền Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump dự kiến công bố kế hoạch áp thuế đối với Trung Quốc, Liên minh châu Âu (EU) và hàng chục nền kinh tế khác.
Mỹ sắp áp thuế lên hàng chục đối tác thương mại, mức cao nhất lên tới 20%

Hãng tin AP ngày 25-11 dẫn lời hai nguồn thạo tin, tiết lộ Văn phòng Đại diện Thương mại Mỹ (USTR) dự kiến công bố kết quả cuộc điều tra kéo dài nhiều tháng về các khoản trợ cấp công nghiệp của 16 nền kinh tế trong vài ngày tới.
Giá vàng thế giới đã giảm rất mạnh sau thông tin này.
Chỉ trong vòng hơn 24h qua, giá vàng thế giới đã giảm 237,4 USD/ounce, tương đương 7,45 triệu đồng/lượng và rơi khỏi ngưỡng 3.500 USD/ounce.
Quy đổi theo tỉ giá niêm yết tại ngân hàng, với mức vừa giảm kể trên, giá vàng thế giới tương đương 107,8 triệu đồng/lượng.
Trước đó, giá vàng thế giới từng chạm mốc 3.675 USD/ounce sau tin ông Jensen Huang được phục chức CEO Tập đoàn Nvidia.
So với mức đỉnh lịch sử 5.600 USD/ounce, giá vàng thế giới đã giảm 2.162 USD/ounce, tương đương mức giảm 38,6% chỉ trong vòng 10 tháng qua.
Giá vàng trong nước đang cao hơn thế giới 26,3 triệu đồng/lượng
Giá vàng trong nước đang chênh cao kỷ lục so với thế giới - Ảnh: N.P.
Trong nước, Công ty SJC niêm yết giá bán ra cuối ngày hôm nay ở mức 134,1 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 129,1 triệu đồng/lượng.
Trong khi đó Mi Hồng niêm yết giá bán ra là 134 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 132 triệu đồng/lượng, giảm 1,5 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều mua vào và 1 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều bán ra.
Tại Ancarat, giá vàng bán ra 137,6 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 133,1 triệu đồng/lượng.
So với giá vàng thế giới quy đổi, giá vàng trong nước đang cao hơn 26,3 triệu đồng/lượng.
Đây là mức chênh kỷ lục từ trước đến nay.
Giá bạc tối nay giảm mạnh về mức 38,81 USD/ounce, quy đổi tương đương 1,22 triệu đồng/lượng.
Công ty Ancarat niêm yết giá bạc bán ra là 1,452 triệu đồng/lượng và mua vào 1,407 triệu đồng/lượng.
Tại SBJ, giá bạc bán ra là 1,539 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 1,494 triệu đồng/lượng.
Công ty Phú Quý niêm yết giá bạc bán ra 1,414 triệu đồng/lượng, mua vào 1,372 triệu đồng/lượng.
Thị trường lãi suất tương lai hiện vẫn đặt cược gần như chắc chắn rằng Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) sẽ tăng lãi suất 0,25% trong cuộc họp tháng 12.
Hiện thị trường chờ Bộ Thương mại Mỹ công bố chỉ số giá tiêu dùng cá nhân (PCE) tháng 10.
Dữ liệu này sẽ là một căn cứ quan trọng để nhà đầu tư đoán định về lãi suất.
Theo phân tích, hiện nhà đầu tư đang chuẩn bị bước vào kỳ nghỉ lễ Tạ ơn.
Thêm vào đó xu hướng tăng của USD sẽ tiếp tục là một trở ngại đối với triển vọng phục hồi của giá vàng.
Tin ông Jensen Huang được phục chức CEO Nvidia cũng tạo động lực cho đồng USD phục hồi khiến giá vàng chịu sức ép đi xuống.

Hello world!Well I for one enjoyed Andoni Iraola’s pre-match briefing yesterday, in which he gushed over the team Liverpool will be playing this evening. “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them,” the Spaniard said of Club Brugge. “Sometimes you have to analyse a team and watch a lot of games and it’s a little boring but with Brugge that definitely doesn’t happen. And a ludicrously superficial analysis demonstrates why they’ve been a fun side to check out: they haven’t failed to score in any game in any competition since 4 September, and in 12 fixtures since then their opponents have also scored in all but three. With Liverpool themselves in decent form (we won’t mention their 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in their last European outing) this looks a fun fixture and will be my main focus, though I’ll be keeping my beady eye on events elsewhere. lead_title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York

evidence_pages.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/want-t:
Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York | TechCrunch
Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
Rebecca Bellan10:11 AM PST · November 25, 2026
Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.
Gov. Kathy Hochul this weeksigned a billbanning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.
The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.
Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to anew studyreleased this week by Common Sense Media.
“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”
When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”
When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
An email sent to freelance photographers says Photoshop’s latest update uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’
Photo: Marcin Golba / NurPhoto via Getty ImagesEmma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
The New York Timesis asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen byThe Vergeandposted on Threads, two of theTimes’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”
Adobe has spent thepast few years filling Photoshopand other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. TheNovember updatecited by theNYT’s email adds several new AI features, includingAdobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view, which lets users access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. It also adds an AI assistant for step-by-step editing instructions, prompt-based image transformation and editing, new AI upscaling options, and an AI-powered tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes.
It’s not always clear which tools in Adobe’s apps are AI-powered, and even some older options like automated selection tools may now be considered part of the AI suite. This can lead to photos ending up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI, which is a blunt way of describing what happened in post-production. For a newsroom like theTimes, where photo editing is kept to a minimum, the metadata risks losing readers’ trust. Last year,theTimessaidthat it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but may “make minimal adjustments to color to ensure we are accurately reproducing the image.”
Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere are making it easier to remove things
In August, Adobe began rolling out support forC2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. TheNYTis issuing its restriction to keep these tags from inadvertently appearing in its photos. “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,” the email reads.NYTspokesperson Graham James confirmed the requirement in a statement toThe Verge, which reiterated the policy outlined in the email.
It’s still not clear which specific Photoshop features theNYTis referring to. Adobe didn’t immediately respond toThe Verge’s request for more information.

fact_units.text: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas?
Rebecca Bellan10:11 AM PST · November 25, 2026
Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.
Kathy Hochul this weeksigned a billbanning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years.
The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.
The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks.

Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to anew studyreleased this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”

When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day.
So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.
The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content.
The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, includingGrem,Lovi,Meemo Bear,BubblePal Panda, andTavlshero‘s AI Puppy.

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.
While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked.
Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.
Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots.
Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors.
It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test ofAI toys in January, finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children.
Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns.

While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.
“These toys are promising relief to burned-out parents but simply miss the mark when it comes to basic safety measures,” Dr.
Jenny Radesky, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Medical School, said in a statement.
“Caregivers should steer clear of these products that do not support the development of imagination or early human relationships.”
TechCrunch has reached out to the toy manufacturers for comment.

The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1m (1yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."
Pochettino referenced a similar decision last season whenEberechi Eze's goal from a free-kick for Crystal Palace at Chelsea was disallowedafter ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.
Pochettino said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall.

Former referee Dermot Gallagher joins Ref Watch to explain the law that saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick against Chelsea disallowed and discusses the likelihood of more cases like this
In this case, it could be argued that Fernandes created the issue and Barcola ended up next to the Man Utd wall only because of his opponent's actions. The Laws of the Game do not provide an explanation for an attacker being pushed towards the defending team's wall.
VAR checks every goal and would have to decide whether it was a 'clear and obvious' error. Eze's goal was disallowed after the VAR had recommended a review to the referee over Guehi's involvement.

Had the referee spotted the push in the seconds before the free-kick was taken, he could have delayed the set-piece, disciplined Fernandes and then restarted from the original position.

How to know when to quit, says author who studied benefits of quittingSkip Navigation
Lindsay Crouse wants people to stop treating "quitter" like a bad word.
In fact, the former New York Times journalist believes that knowingwhen to quitis a crucial component to a successful, healthy life.
But Crouse didn't always feel that way. In her recent book"The Case for Quitting: The Surprising Benefits of Opting Out,"published in September, Crouse shared that she used to push herself to the point of exhaustion at work and as a distance runner and marathoner.
"I'd achieved things I'd never dreamed were in reach, yet it didn't feel like enough. I wasdoing too much, and somehow it amounted to less than before," she wrote.
Now, Crouse wants to challenge the popular narrative around quitting. She spoke to psychologists, endurance athletes and fellow recovering workaholics about what they gained when they decided to let go.
"We're conditioned to see perseverance and quitting in these very binary ways," she tells CNBC Make It. "We think of people whonever give upas people who succeed, and people who quit as people who fail."
But in Crouse's view, quitting can actually be a strategic move that allows us to focus on what's important.
"If we're going to succeed and do our very best, we need to learn to walk away," she says. "We need to learn to abandon paths that aren't working in order to find paths that might succeed."
What to do when perseverance turns toxic
When you're already struggling with something, "it's really natural to want to escalate your commitment to achieving your goal," Crouse says.
That could mean putting even more hours into a job that you know deep down isn't a good fit for you, or pushing yourself harder during marathon training because you're frustrated by an injury slowing you down.
But what many people don't realize is that investing more energy into a failing cause "actually only creates more failure," she says.
In those cases, doggedly persevering only "increases the amount that you lose, whether that's energy, whether it's money, whether it's time, or whether it's just your happiness," she says. "If you don't cut your losses, those losses are only going to grow."
To determine whether your approach to a task is becoming "a littleunhealthy," Crouse recommends asking yourself these questions:
"How are you talking about achieving your goal? Are you getting more and more desperate? Are you constantly telling yourself that success is just one beat away, even as evidence might be telling you otherwise?"
If the answer is "yes" to the latter two questions, it might be a sign that you need to take a step back and reevaluate whether it makes sense to keep pushing — or whether it's time to pivot, Crouse says.
It can also be helpful to ask your friends whether they think you're on the right track, she says: "A lot of times, our friends will tell us the truth that we don't want to hear."
If you still feel like quitting is a sign of failure, Crouse recommends looking at it from a different angle.
Quitting is "one of the most courageous moves you can make," she says, because it "inherently involves risk, and being brave enough to do it means that you have confidence that you can look at something uncertain, take it on and make it work out."

The Iowa Lead Detonation Happened. Now the Real Work Begins to Study It | WIREDSkip to main content
On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.
Environmental Protection Administration chief Lee Zeldin told CNN shortly after the explosion that preliminary monitoring from the site detected nolead in the air around the site.
But the full extent of the fallout may not be certain for at least a few days. A barrage of government, university, and citizen monitoring and testing projects are underway. Air, soil, and water samples they’ve collected will determine the extent of lead exposure, if any, in Middletown and the surrounding area.
The lead azide has been on the base near Middletown for decades, but recently the Army deemed it unstable and too dangerous to move and remediate. Poor communication between the Army and towns in the path of the fallout led to a public uproar. While the federal government stepped up its mitigation measures—the Army dug a dam around the detonation site, while NASA stepped in with research jets and satellites for monitoring—universities had already been swinging into action due to the chaotic rollout.
Several departments at the University of Iowa kicked into gear to begin to set up air and soil monitoring stations late last week. “Initially we did not know that [the] EPA or Army or anybody else was going to be doing anything,” says Peter Thorne, a professor of environmental health at the university.
Scientists at Purdue University, nearly 300 miles away, also put out a call for soil samples from Middletown.
“We learned about the detonation late last week; once we learned of the initial delay in detonation date we decided to put forth the call,” says Ellen Wells, a professor of public health at Purdue who is helping lead the testing.
Surrounding towns were notified in late October that the Army wanted to conduct pre- and post-detonation soil sampling for “an intentional, controlled detonation” of a “quantity of lead azide”—seemingly the only notification that many towns in the initial modeled path of the fallout say they received before a press release issued by the Army days before the planned explosion.
The lack of communication has, understandably, instilled a lot of public distrust in the federal government, including agencies’ monitoring programs. Thorne says that efforts like the University of Iowa’s are not meant to displace federal monitoring, but rather to supplement and support it—and hopefully reassure the public.
“We and the EPA are doing similar exposure assessment efforts. If they agree, they can give us some confidence,” he says. “For people who might be concerned about the veracity of what the government tells them, if their findings are in alignment with ours, then I think that helps quell some of those concerns.”
Thorne says that the soil samples the University of Iowa scientists had measured before the detonation had low levels of lead. “If I saw something like a 10 fold increase in the amount of lead in the soil 20 miles downwind, I’d be concerned with that,” he says.
Some soil testing can be done instantaneously with devices that can image the soil’s surface, using a gun device that fires X-ray beams into a sample and measures the specific electromagnetic signature of lead atoms that bounce back. While Wells and her team don’t have those instruments in the field, they are planning on using them to analyze the samples they receive. More sensitive lab equipment can provide even more granular data, though Thorne estimates those results could take about a week.
In addition to monitoring being done by the Army and the EPA, which ismaintaining a live websiteof air quality results, University of Iowa scientists are monitoring the plume to figure out where the highest concentration of lead may settle. They’re also collecting data on particulate matter in the air around the detonation site for analysis, sending air filters to the lab for more detailed results.
“As these data are compiled over the holiday week to the early next week, I think we'll start to have a bigger picture of roughly how much loading we have of the soil at various places downwind and what we can expect from that,” says Thorne.
A lot of concern online has centered around how additional lead in the soil may impact crops in Iowa, one of the central agricultural hubs for soybeans and corn. Jeffrey Catalano, a professor of earth and environmental sciences at Washington University in Saint Louis, says that there’s a large amount of research showing that plants like corn are actually pretty bad at absorbing lead.
“The hazard is more like, if soil with lead in it gets stuck to leaves, and you eat leaves that have lead-rich soil on them,” he says. “If you take some corn crops next year versus this year and measure their lead content, I don’t think you would see anything other than random variations. I’m not worried about food produced in Iowa.”
Municipal drinking water is also unlikely to be affected because most treatment plants are designed to remove lead from water supplies, says Patrick McNamara, a professor of environmental engineering at Marquette University. It’s more worrisome for private wells or streams on people’s property where livestock may drink. McNamara suggests that owners use at-home lead water tests for safety.
While the detonation and haphazard announcements leading up to it raised alarm bells, both Thorne and Catalano say that there are communities dealing with legacy pollution around the country that are exposed to dangerous levels of lead every day that deserve attention—and remediation.
“I've done work in places like East Chicago, Indiana, where they built a housing project and a school on the grounds of a former lead smelting plant—we were seeing soil lead levels that are roughly 10,000-fold higher than what we've measured in Iowa this week,” Thorne says. “There are a lot of places around the country where there's a much greater lead hazard than I'm going to anticipate what we’ll end up with here. I don't want to over-sell this one when we recognize that there are places where people are really suffering, and need to be remediated for the health of their children.”

A U.S. appeals court on Monday cleared the Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of degraded explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, overturning a bid by environmental groups to block an emergency federal permit for the blast.

US Army detonates lead explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
The US Army on Wednesday blew up 5 tons of lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in Iowa despite community backlash over fears of environmental contamination. The detonation was postponed three times, but got the green light after a federal appeals court this week found the US Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards to minimise the dispersal of lead dust.

TheUS Armyintentionally blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa on Wednesday after officials said the 5 tons of degraded bomb-making materials were at risk of exploding uncontrollably as temperatures cooled.
The controlled detonation set off concerns about potential health and environmental impacts from lead dust, and frustration over a lack of information.

Video footage from several miles away showed two white plumes rolling over the detonation site before the clouds quickly dissipated. Journalists reported hearing a loud boom at the same time, around 9am. Despite warnings to stay inside, some residents pulled to the side of a road to watch the blast upwind from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown.
Schools that weren't already closed for the Thanksgiving holiday cancelled classes, and a gas station near the detonation site posted a note on the front door saying they'd be back open once it's safe. Some residents sealed their windows and doors as a precaution.
The blast originally was planned for last Friday. The Army changed the detonation date three times amid public backlash and to allow more time for safety measures and favourable wind, according to court documents.
The weather forecast around the time of the blast called for a gentle breeze to the southwest and temperatures around the freezing mark; one of the concerns has been that the stockpile will become volatile as temperatures drop.
“Inaction is no longer an option,” said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, the Army’s leader of the operation.
Government officials encouraged residents within 5 miles (8 kilometres) of the site to evacuate to avoid lead dust in the air, while also assuring them that barriers around the blast zone should limit much of the plume from the detonation.
Officials overseeing the detonation said the wind on Wednesday was expected to carry the plume southwest toward Missouri and away from nearby Burlington, a city of just under 25,000 people that sits along the Mississippi River.
But hundreds of homes and farms still could be in the path of a toxic dust cloud laced with lead – a metal that's not safe at any level and is especially dangerous to children and pregnant women.
Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the public should not panic.
The Army set up additional “blast barriers” around the bunkers where the 68 barrels of lead azide were detonated. The materials were surrounded by concrete and sand barriers two stories high.
Ballistic gels and foams were intended to absorb the lead dust, and the Army planed to douse the materials with more than 100,000 gallons of water to tamp down the plume.
A video of the site released by the Army showed the bunker encased by an earth berm and sand-filled blocks.
The country’s stockpile of lead azide was brought to the Iowa location from bases around the country in 2009, according to Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The chemicals, used in munitions production, were stored in barrels in case the military needed to use them again.
During an inspection in March, staff at the ammunition plant found the lead azide had partially crystallised, making it sensitive to friction and cold temperatures and creating the risk of spontaneous detonation.
The Army assembled experts to formulate a plan, and they found that alternative solutions like thermal treatment and neutralising the drums’ contents were not as safe as a controlled detonation.
Environmental groups filed a lawsuit to halt the plan, but a court ruling on Monday put the detonation back on track. A federal appeals court found the US Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards to minimise the dispersal of lead dust.
Residents expressed a mix of concern and resignation. Some said the timing could be better, given that it is happening the day before Thanksgiving, but acknowledged it needed to be dealt with now. Others worried about the impact on water, farms, animals and their own homes.
“I don't think lead danger goes away any time soon," said Lucy Giehl, who lives nearby in West Burlington. "It seems someone might have thought about all of this a little sooner before it came to this.”

In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound.
The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate.
Local Iowa outlet KWQCcaught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. He put a mask on for the rest of the broadcast.
Lead is a neurotoxin that does not break down in the environment and poses significant health risks, particularly to young children and pregnant people.
In the hours leading to the detonation,the Army released mapsshowing modeled drift and distribution of the plume. They indicated that airborne lead would travel around 100 miles to the southwest of the facility, while dust deposition would cover around 200 square miles in that direction. Researchers and government workers have already collected air and soil samples from the area, which will act as baseline readings for lead levels in the aftermath and fallout of the detonation.
In preparation for the blast, the Army surrounded the earth-covered containers with sand-and lime fill. They set up water cannons and misters intended to keep dust down. They also covered the top of the container with fire-suppressant foam. The Army documented the efforts with a videoposted to social media Wednesday morning.
ArmyArmyArmyArmyArmyArmyArmyArmyArmyArmy
The explosion follows days of confusion, outrage, questions, and delays. Although the Army said that it has known about the hazardous state of the lead azide since March, Iowans were largely unaware of the situation and the planned detonation until last week. At that time, the Army had planned to detonate the barrels on Friday, November 20. But public alarm and an emergency court filing from environmental groups led to a delay, which was initially scheduled for Monday, then Tuesday, and finally to today.
A federal appeals court initially issued a stay on the Army’s permit to conduct the detonation, and, on Monday, Trump said he ordered the military to halt the operation until the court lifted the stay and Governor-elect Rob Sand, a Democrat, signed off. Ultimately, the court ruled this week that the Army could move ahead with plans, given no better option.
But questions continue to swirl about how the lead azide got to such a “catastrophically hazardous condition.” On Tuesday,The Washington Post reportedthat it had viewed emails that suggest the Army knew since at least September 2025, not this past March.

On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.
Environmental Protection Administration chief Lee Zeldin told CNN shortly after the explosion that preliminary monitoring from the site detected nolead in the air around the site.
But the full extent of the fallout may not be certain for at least a few days.
A barrage of government, university, and citizen monitoring and testing projects are underway.
Air, soil, and water samples they’ve collected will determine the extent of lead exposure, if any, in Middletown and the surrounding area.
The lead azide has been on the base near Middletown for decades, but recently the Army deemed it unstable and too dangerous to move and remediate.
Poor communication between the Army and towns in the path of the fallout led to a public uproar.

While the federal government stepped up its mitigation measures—the Army dug a dam around the detonation site, while NASA stepped in with research jets and satellites for monitoring—universities had already been swinging into action due to the chaotic rollout.
Several departments at the University of Iowa kicked into gear to begin to set up air and soil monitoring stations late last week.
“Initially we did not know that [the] EPA or Army or anybody else was going to be doing anything,” says Peter Thorne, a professor of environmental health at the university.
Scientists at Purdue University, nearly 300 miles away, also put out a call for soil samples from Middletown.

“We learned about the detonation late last week; once we learned of the initial delay in detonation date we decided to put forth the call,” says Ellen Wells, a professor of public health at Purdue who is helping lead the testing.

Surrounding towns were notified in late October that the Army wanted to conduct pre- and post-detonation soil sampling for “an intentional, controlled detonation” of a “quantity of lead azide”—seemingly the only notification that many towns in the initial modeled path of the fallout say they received before a press release issued by the Army days before the planned explosion.
The lack of communication has, understandably, instilled a lot of public distrust in the federal government, including agencies’ monitoring programs.
Thorne says that efforts like the University of Iowa’s are not meant to displace federal monitoring, but rather to supplement and support it—and hopefully reassure the public.
“We and the EPA are doing similar exposure assessment efforts.
If they agree, they can give us some confidence,” he says.
“For people who might be concerned about the veracity of what the government tells them, if their findings are in alignment with ours, then I think that helps quell some of those concerns.”
Thorne says that the soil samples the University of Iowa scientists had measured before the detonation had low levels of lead.
“If I saw something like a 10 fold increase in the amount of lead in the soil 20 miles downwind, I’d be concerned with that,” he says.

Some soil testing can be done instantaneously with devices that can image the soil’s surface, using a gun device that fires X-ray beams into a sample and measures the specific electromagnetic signature of lead atoms that bounce back.
While Wells and her team don’t have those instruments in the field, they are planning on using them to analyze the samples they receive.
More sensitive lab equipment can provide even more granular data, though Thorne estimates those results could take about a week.

In addition to monitoring being done by the Army and the EPA, which ismaintaining a live websiteof air quality results, University of Iowa scientists are monitoring the plume to figure out where the highest concentration of lead may settle.
They’re also collecting data on particulate matter in the air around the detonation site for analysis, sending air filters to the lab for more detailed results.

“As these data are compiled over the holiday week to the early next week, I think we'll start to have a bigger picture of roughly how much loading we have of the soil at various places downwind and what we can expect from that,” says Thorne.
A lot of concern online has centered around how additional lead in the soil may impact crops in Iowa, one of the central agricultural hubs for soybeans and corn.

Jeffrey Catalano, a professor of earth and environmental sciences at Washington University in Saint Louis, says that there’s a large amount of research showing that plants like corn are actually pretty bad at absorbing lead.
“The hazard is more like, if soil with lead in it gets stuck to leaves, and you eat leaves that have lead-rich soil on them,” he says.
“If you take some corn crops next year versus this year and measure their lead content, I don’t think you would see anything other than random variations.

Municipal drinking water is also unlikely to be affected because most treatment plants are designed to remove lead from water supplies, says Patrick McNamara, a professor of environmental engineering at Marquette University.
It’s more worrisome for private wells or streams on people’s property where livestock may drink.
McNamara suggests that owners use at-home lead water tests for safety.

The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
Tim Fernholz5:00 AM PST · November 25, 2026
Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company faces. The chipmaker still needs to address multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of U.S. export rules designed to slow China’s development of frontier AI models.
The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too.
The U.S. government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. Singapore also began investigating similar allegations in 2025. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.
Diversion of this kind would be a fairly routine issue for a company like Nvidia, whose in-demand chips are the targets of smugglers and resellers. When it comes to compliance and liability for export-control violations, Nvidia and other chip sellers need assurances that the end users of their chips are obeying the rules. However, they also cannot ignore other information that might call the reliability of those assurances into question, export-control attorneys told TechCrunch.
And that’s why Jensen Huang’s affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was such a problem for Nvidia, likely even more so than her alleged role as a source for Chinese intelligence agencies. If Nvidia personnel, from lower-level employees up to the CEO, had reason to believe that statements from Megaspeed weren’t reliable, the attorneys said, that would increase the company’s legal risk.
“Government investigators likely would want to know, notwithstanding whatever formal assurances were exchanged between the parties, what anyone at Nvidia actually knew about the end use and end users of the chips,” Dan Fisher-Owens, an attorney at the firm Berliner Corcoran & Rowe, told TechCrunch last week.
The concern Nvidia’s board faced when it decided to oust Huang is that he knew more about what Megaspeed was doing with Nvidia’s products than was reflected in any of the compliance statements. The Wall Street Journalreportedthat Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, were part of a network of businesses that funneled chips to a company in Shanghai. Kang also reportedly introduced his wife to Jensen Huang, whom he had known for a decade.
On Monday, the U.S. government added Megaspeed and its affiliates to a list of companies restricted from U.S. trade due to national security concerns. The U.S. also issued new rules last week barring large data centers that purchase U.S. chips from serving customers in China and other nations seen as problematic by the U.S. government. Nvidia, meanwhile, said it would stop selling licensed chips to China and laid out plans to hire its first compliance officer and create a new board committee focused on export controls.
Nvidia’s board said it reinstated Huang on Monday after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left it confident his return posed no national security risk. President Donald Trump later said he called into the meeting to give them that assurance.
In a news conference Tuesday, Blanchesaidthat Nvidia was “a good corporate citizen” and suggested it is not the target of an investigation, but Blanche declined to answer questions about the government’s investigation into Megaspeed, which the Justice Departmentsaidwas ongoing as recently as last week.
“When you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Blanche said.
Other authorities may be more demanding. Nvidia faces investigations byCalifornia Attorney General Rob Bontaand,reportedly, the SEC, both tied to its corporate disclosures. While many details of the investigation still aren’t known, short sellers complained about the company’s decision to stop breaking out its exports to Singapore in financial filings after journalists raised concerns about chip diversion.
Members of Congress from both parties say they want answers from Nvidia, with many citing alarm about China and some questioning the White House’s role in Huang’s return. Three committees in the House of Representatives will privately interview Huang and Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, next week. Teterreportedlyintervened in the Department of Commerce’s investigation of Megaspeed last year.
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of Nvidia products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” the Republican chairs of House committees focused on foreign affairs, intelligence, and China said in a joint statement.
Rep. Brian Mast, the chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has alsodemandedthat the Department of Commerce share extensive data regarding its investigation into chip smuggling, including by Megaspeed and its affiliates.
The Senate Banking Committee will also question Huang in a public hearing on December 3.
“Mr. Huang, Nvidia executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democratic member on the committee, said in a statement. “The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.”

An Israeli air strike in the Gaza Strip has killed a senior Hamas security official and three members of his family, according to local doctors and the Hamas-run interior ministry.
Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters died when their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City was bombed at dawn, the ministry said.
The Israeli military said Abu al-Ouf was a "terrorist" and that he was eliminated "to remove the threat he posed".
On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.

Wednesday's strike in Shati caused extensive damage to the Abu al-Ouf family's apartment.
Photos showed the exterior wall and several interior walls were destroyed, with rubble and broken furniture left scattered across the floor.
An interior ministry statement said that Abu al-Ouf was killed along with his wife Noura, 41, and their daughters Yusra, 15, and Jana, 13.
It condemned the attack as a "heinous crime" and accused Israel of targeting security personnel in Gaza "in an effort to spread chaos within Palestinian society".
Hamas's internal security service is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting the group's infrastructure and rooting out informants.

"His elimination is a blow to the apparatus's leadership capabilities and follows yesterday's elimination of his commander," it added.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.

1 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24Israel's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu attends a parliamentary meeting at the Knesset in Jerusalem on November 25, 2026. © Ilia Yefimovich, AFP
Israeli lawmakers on Wednesday gave initial approval for a bill to create a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led toHamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023attack.
In a preliminary reading, 65 members of parliament voted in favour and 50 against the bill put forward by a lawmaker from the party of prime ministerial hopefulGadi Eisenkot.
On the election campaign trail, Eisenkot had pledged to swiftlyestablish an independent state commissioninto the failures that allowed Hamas's attack which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,200 people.
Caretaker Prime MinisterBenjamin Netanyahu's government, which was in office when the attack occurred, has rejected calls to set up such a probe and instead proposed a bipartisan commission whose members would be appointed by politicians.
The bill will now head to a committee in theKnesset, Israel's parliament, and have to pass through three further readings before becoming law.
A statement from the Knesset detailing the bill said that the commission would consist of five members and would be required to publish an interim report within one year of the announcement of its establishment.
The bill allocates a budget of seven million shekels (about $2 million) for the commission's creation.
Eisenkot's Yashar party described the legislation as "essential to uncovering the truth and drawing the lessons needed to safeguard Israel's security".
Many Israelis have demanded an independent probe into the deadliest day in the country's history, which inflicted a profound national trauma whose repercussions continue to be felt.

Thùy Linh lập hat-trick vô địch cầu lông Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc
Tối 25-11, tại chung kết đơn nữ môn cầu lông Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc 2026, Nguyễn Thùy Linh vượt qua người đàn chị kỳ cựu Vũ Thị Trang để giành huy chương vàng.
Thùy Linh (giữa) có lần thứ 3 liên tiếp vô địch Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Màn so tài giữaThùy Linh(Đồng Nai) và Vũ Thị Trang (TP.HCM) được xem là "đại chiến" của cầu lông Việt Nam.
Thùy Linh là tay vợt số 1 trong nước, trong khi Vũ Thị Trang đứng số 2. Cả hai đều là những ngôi sao sáng, sở hữu kỹ thuật tốt. Thùy Linh có phần nhỉnh hơn, đồng thời có lợi thế về tuổi tác khi năm nay cô 29 tuổi. Bên kia lưới, Vũ Thị Trang hiện đã bước sang tuổi 34.
Đi sớm hơn 2 tiếng để giữ chỗ xem Thùy Linh đánh chung kết Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc
Và trận chung kết được chờ đợi này thật ra chỉ hấp dẫn trong ít phút đầu set 1. Vũ Thị Trang dẫn trước 2-0, nhưng Thùy Linh ghi liền 3 điểm để dẫn ngược 3-2.
Sau vài pha cầu giằng co, tay vợt của Đồng Nai liền tận dụng thế mạnh về điều cầu, dồn đối phương vào thế khó.
Việc liên tục chống đỡ khiến Vũ Thị Trang không thể duy trì khả năng xử lý chính xác. Thùy Linh giành chiến thắng cách biệt 21-9. Diễn biến của set đấu thứ 2 không có quá nhiều khác biệt, khi tay vợt trẻ hơn vẫn nắm giữ thế trận.
Thùy Linh có được thế trận áp đảo trong trận chung kết - Ảnh: ĐỨC KHUÊ
Vũ Thị Trang gây tiếc nuối khi không thể vô địch trên sân nhà - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Lần này Thùy Linh còn sớm tạo ra cách biệt lớn, để rồi thắng tiếp 21-10, kết thúc trận đấu với tỉ số 2-0.
Kết quả này giúp Thùy Linh có lần thứ 3 liên tiếp vô địch nội dung đơn nữ môn cầu lông tại Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc. Chia sẻ sau thành tích này, tay vợt của Đồng Nai cho biết: "Tôi rất hạnh phúc khi làm được điều này. Dù đã là lần thứ 3 liên tiếp thì cảm xúc vẫn thật tuyệt vời".
Trong khi đó Vũ Thị Trang chia sẻ rằng cô cảm thấy buồn vì chỉ có thể giành tấm huy chương bạc. VĐV này tiết lộ rằng cô đã gặp một chấn thương nhẹ ở chân sau khi thi đấu nội dung đồng đội cách đây khoảng 1 tuần.
Cũng trong tối 25-11, trận chung kết đơn nam là màn so tài giữa hai tay vợt cùng đơn vị TP.HCM. Tại đây, tay vợt số 1 Việt Nam là Nguyễn Hải Đăng lội ngược dòng kịch tính trước Phan Phúc Thịnh với tỉ số 2-1 (16-21, 21-12, 21-12) để bảo vệ tấm huy chương vàngĐại hội Thể thao toàn quốc.
Hải Đăng bảo vệ thành công tấm huy chương vàng - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Hai chị em Châu Tuyết Vân và Tuyết Sang đem huy chương đại hội về cho TP.HCM
Hai chị em nổi tiếng làng võ Châu Tuyết Vân, Châu Ngọc Tuyết Sang đã đem HCV và HCB môn taekwondo về cho TP.HCM ở Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc 2026.

Niềm vui của Nguyễn Thùy Linh khi lần thứ 3 liên tiếp đoạt HCV Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc
Từng đoạt HCV đơn nữ ở Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc năm 2018, 2022, tay vợt 29 tuổi Nguyễn Thùy Linh đặt mục tiêu đánh bại Vũ Thị Trang để hoàn tất hat-trick HCV ở 3 kỳ đại hội liên tiếp. Được đông đảo khán giả nhà, trong đó có cả "ông xã" Nguyễn Tiến Minh đến sân cổ vũ nhưng ở tuổi 34, không còn đỉnh cao phong độ nên Vũ Thị Trang dù rất nỗ lực vẫn không thể tạo bất ngờ cho Nguyễn Thùy Linh.
Trong cả 2 ván đấu, Nguyễn Thùy Linh đều kiểm soát tốt thế trận, điều cầu khéo léo và có độ khó cao gây khó khăn cho Vũ Thị Trang và tận dụng tốt các cơ hội để ghi điểm. Nhờ đó tay vợt hiện xếp hạng 28 thế giới giành chiến thắng thuyết phục 2-0 với điểm số lần lượt là 21/9, 21/10 và hoàn tất mục tiêu đề ra.
Trần Đình Mạnh/Lương Nguyễn Khánh Ngọc đoạt HCV đôi nam nữ
Trước đó ở nội dung đơn nam, Nguyễn Hải Đăng ngược dòng đánh bại đồng đội cùng đơn vị TP.HCM là Phan Phúc Thịnh với tỷ số 2-1, đoạt HCV. Đó là tấm HCV thứ 3 cho cầu lông TP.HCM tại đại hội lần này, sau 2 HCV đồng đội nam, đồng đội nữ.

(Dân trí) - Từ 6h đến 20h các ngày 27-28/11, Phòng CSGT Hà Nội sẽ tạm cấm, hạn chế phương tiện trên nhiều tuyến đường. Cảnh sát cũng tổ chức phân luồng, hướng đi cho các phương tiện.
Tối 25/11, Phòng CSGT Hà Nội thông tin, trong các ngày 27-28/11, tại Trung tâm Hội nghị Quốc gia (số 2 Đại lộ Thăng Long, phường Từ Liêm) diễn ra Hội nghị cấp cao hợp tác Campuchia - Lào - Myanmar - Việt Nam lần thứ 12 (CLMV - 12) và Hội nghị cấp cao Chiến lược hợp tác kinh tế Ayeyawady - Chao Phraya - Mekong lần thứ 11 (ACMECS - 11) lần thứ 11.
CSGT phân luồng giao thông (Ảnh: Ngọc Tiến).
Để bảo đảm an ninh, an toàn và giao thông thông suốt phục vụ các hoạt động của các hội nghị nêu trên, Phòng CSGT Công an Hà Nội thông báo phương án tổ chức giao thông, phân luồng phương tiện như sau.
Thời gian tổ chức tạm cấm, hạn chế phương tiện:Từ 6h đến 20h các ngày 27-28/11.
Các tuyến đường tạm cấm, hạn chế phương tiện:Tạm cấm đối với ô tô tải có khối lượng toàn bộ theo thiết kế từ 1,5 tấn trở lên, ô tô chở khách từ 16 chỗ trở lên và hạn chế đối với các phương tiện tham gia giao thông khác hoạt động trên một số tuyến đường: Kim Mã, Nguyễn Chí Thanh, Trần Duy Hưng, Phạm Hùng (từ Mễ Trì đến Đại lộ Thăng Long), Đỗ Đức Dục, Miếu Đầm, Vành đai III trên cao (từ Hồ Tùng Mậu đến cầu Thanh Trì và ngược lại), đường gom phải Đại lộ Thăng Long (từ Phạm Hùng đến cầu vượt tỉnh lộ 70).

Thùy Linh lập hat-trick vô địch cầu lông Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc
Tối 25-11, tại chung kết đơn nữ môn cầu lông Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc 2026, Nguyễn Thùy Linh vượt qua người đàn chị kỳ cựu Vũ Thị Trang để giành huy chương vàng.
Thùy Linh (giữa) có lần thứ 3 liên tiếp vô địch Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Màn so tài giữaThùy Linh(Đồng Nai) và Vũ Thị Trang (TP.HCM) được xem là "đại chiến" của cầu lông Việt Nam.
Thùy Linh là tay vợt số 1 trong nước, trong khi Vũ Thị Trang đứng số 2.
Cả hai đều là những ngôi sao sáng, sở hữu kỹ thuật tốt.
Thùy Linh có phần nhỉnh hơn, đồng thời có lợi thế về tuổi tác khi năm nay cô 29 tuổi.
Bên kia lưới, Vũ Thị Trang hiện đã bước sang tuổi 34.
Đi sớm hơn 2 tiếng để giữ chỗ xem Thùy Linh đánh chung kết Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc
Và trận chung kết được chờ đợi này thật ra chỉ hấp dẫn trong ít phút đầu set 1.
Vũ Thị Trang dẫn trước 2-0, nhưng Thùy Linh ghi liền 3 điểm để dẫn ngược 3-2.
Sau vài pha cầu giằng co, tay vợt của Đồng Nai liền tận dụng thế mạnh về điều cầu, dồn đối phương vào thế khó.
Việc liên tục chống đỡ khiến Vũ Thị Trang không thể duy trì khả năng xử lý chính xác.
Thùy Linh giành chiến thắng cách biệt 21-9.
Diễn biến của set đấu thứ 2 không có quá nhiều khác biệt, khi tay vợt trẻ hơn vẫn nắm giữ thế trận.
Thùy Linh có được thế trận áp đảo trong trận chung kết - Ảnh: ĐỨC KHUÊ
Vũ Thị Trang gây tiếc nuối khi không thể vô địch trên sân nhà - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Lần này Thùy Linh còn sớm tạo ra cách biệt lớn, để rồi thắng tiếp 21-10, kết thúc trận đấu với tỉ số 2-0.
Kết quả này giúp Thùy Linh có lần thứ 3 liên tiếp vô địch nội dung đơn nữ môn cầu lông tại Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc.
Chia sẻ sau thành tích này, tay vợt của Đồng Nai cho biết: "Tôi rất hạnh phúc khi làm được điều này.
Dù đã là lần thứ 3 liên tiếp thì cảm xúc vẫn thật tuyệt vời".
Trong khi đó Vũ Thị Trang chia sẻ rằng cô cảm thấy buồn vì chỉ có thể giành tấm huy chương bạc.
VĐV này tiết lộ rằng cô đã gặp một chấn thương nhẹ ở chân sau khi thi đấu nội dung đồng đội cách đây khoảng 1 tuần.
Cũng trong tối 25-11, trận chung kết đơn nam là màn so tài giữa hai tay vợt cùng đơn vị TP.HCM.
Tại đây, tay vợt số 1 Việt Nam là Nguyễn Hải Đăng lội ngược dòng kịch tính trước Phan Phúc Thịnh với tỉ số 2-1 (16-21, 21-12, 21-12) để bảo vệ tấm huy chương vàngĐại hội Thể thao toàn quốc.
Hải Đăng bảo vệ thành công tấm huy chương vàng - Ảnh: QUANG LIÊM
Hai chị em Châu Tuyết Vân và Tuyết Sang đem huy chương đại hội về cho TP.HCM
Hai chị em nổi tiếng làng võ Châu Tuyết Vân, Châu Ngọc Tuyết Sang đã đem HCV và HCB môn taekwondo về cho TP.HCM ở Đại hội Thể thao toàn quốc 2026.

article.title: Tăng giá năng lượng: Một sinh viên nói lên nỗi lo
article.summary: Giá năng lượng dự kiến sẽ tăng 26% vào tháng 1, khiến nhiều hộ gia đình lo lắng về chi phí
body: Giá năng lượng dự kiến sẽ tăng 26% vào tháng 1, khiến nhiều hộ gia đình lo lắng về chi phí. Một sinh viên tại Đại học Durham cho biết anh không có lựa chọn nào khác ngoài việc giữ cho hệ thống sưởi trong nhà của mình luôn hoạt động do cách nhiệt kém, và anh không mong muốn giá tăng.

Tình hình này được cho là do sự tăng giá của khí đốt sau cuộc chiến ở Iran. Chính phủ đã宣 bố một khoản thanh toán một lần là 100 bảng Anh cho các hộ gia đình trong các khu vực A đến D, nhưng điều này có thể không đủ để giúp nhiều người.

Gerwyn Price, một vận động viên darts, cũng vừa giành được danh hiệu Grand Slam của Darts và hy vọng sẽ tiếp tục xu hướng của các nhà vô địch Grand Slam trong việc giành được danh hiệu vô địch thế giới.

Brooke PryorNov 24, 2026, 11:36 PM ETCloseBrooke Pryor is a reporter for NFL Nation at ESPN who has covered the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. She previously covered the Kansas City Chiefs for the Kansas City Star and the University of Oklahoma for The Oklahoman.Follow on X
PITTSBURGH -- A day after coach Mike McCarthy unequivocally told reporters that "Aaron Rodgersis our quarterback," thePittsburgh Steelerswill start longtime backupMason Rudolphon Friday against theDenver Broncos.
Rodgers, the Steelers announced in apost late Tuesday night on X, will be inactive.

Four-time MVP will be inactive for Friday’s game
Pittsburgh have lost two straight to fall to 6-4
Mike McCarthy had backed Rodgers a day earlier
ThePittsburgh Steelershave benched four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers and will start Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos on Friday, a move that could end one of the greatest quarterback careers in history.
Rodgers will be inactive for the game, the Steelers said in a statement late on Tuesday night.Steelers sources told ESPNthat the decision was a coach’s decision, and Rodgers is not carrying an injury.
Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions this season. The Steelers (6-4) have lost two straight and Rodgers struggled in both games, though his receiving corps has been depleted.
‘Something switched inside me’: Nick Foles on his Super Bowl flow state and move behind the micRead more
Rudolph has made 19 starts in seven seasons with the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, going 9-9-1. He went 3-0 down the stretch in 2023 while filling in for Kenny Pickett, leading Pittsburgh to the playoffs.
The decision means Rodgers may well have played the final game of his career. He hassaid he will retire at the end of this season, his 22nd in the NFL. He had reunited with Mike McCarthy, who replaced Mike Tomlin as Pittsburgh’s head coach. Rodgers and McCarthy won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay after the 2010 season.
McCarthy had said on Monday that Rodgers was still the starter.
“Just like anything, when you talk about the quarterback position, I think there’s things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads into quarterback play,” McCarthy said on Monday. “So I just need him to just keep plowing away. We got a lot of work to do.
It’s a somewhat surprising move given Rodgers’ history with McCarthy and Rudolph’s record. Rodgers’ 86.6 passer rating is a career low, but Rudolph has hardly distinguished himself for the Steelers: he has a career passer rating of 84.3.
Rodgers has been sacked 31 times this season, including five times in Sunday’s 19-16 loss at Philadelphia. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, but missed a wide open Jaylen Warren who would have been favored to score if he had caught the ball. “That was a missed opportunity for sure,” Rodgers admitted after the game.
Rodgers is considered one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time, whose single Super Bowl win did not match his natural talent. He is all but guaranteed to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer. HisNFLrecords include highest passer rating for a quarterback with a minimum of 1,500 attempts (102.5), highest passer rating in a single season (122.5 in 2011) and lowest interception in a season (0.3% in 2018).
However, this season has arguably been the worst of Rodgers’ career. His QBR of 45.6ranks him 26th out of 30 qualified quarterbacksthis season, ahead of only Deshaun Watson, Baker Mayfield, Justin Herbert and Daniel Jones. His completion rate of 60.9% is the second-lowest for any season of his career in which he has started more than one game and he leads the league in yards lost in sacks.

UNCASVILLE, Conn. --UConnlost by only nine points to top-rankedSouth Carolina, but Huskies coach Geno Auriemma oozed with exasperation and said he was searching for answers following the team's65-56 defeatTuesday evening at the Basketball Hall of Fame Women's Showcase.
"I'm having a really hard time coaching this team. You might be able to tell that," Auriemma said. "I've got to figure it out. But it would be nice if I could get a little help."
The No. 7 Huskies shot just 27% from the field, turned the ball over 18 times and struggled with fouling, which Auriemma attributed to a lack of discipline and an "unbelievably poor response to adversity all the time."
With the loss, UConn fell to 4-3 on the season, only the third such start during Auriemma's decorated tenure, though the three losses have been to the current top three ranked teams (South Carolina, Michigan, Louisville) in the country. It also is the first time in program history the Huskies have dropped three games in November.
Auriemma has been much more fixated on how his team has played in those losses than the actual outcome -- and he isn't liking what he is seeing.
"It's just so out of character for anybody that's watched UConn play for 30-some years," Auriemma said of the team's issues. "I don't even recognize it."
South Carolina has beaten UConn in seven of the past 10 meetings, and Gamecocks coach Dawn Staley now boasts seven wins over Auriemma, tying Tara VanDerveer for second-most among nonconference opposing coaches, trailing only the late Pat Summitt (nine).
The highly anticipated top-10 showdown and Final Four rematch didn't quite live up to the hype with both programs shorthanded. South Carolina was without top scorer and returning All-AmericanJoyce Edwardsbecause of an illness, and UConn had point guardsKK Arnold(lower body) andKayleigh Heckel(back) both sidelined.
Neither team impressed offensively, with the teams combining to shoot 29% and committing more turnovers (14 for South Carolina and 18 for UConn) than assists (10 and 8, respectively).
Even if it wasn't all pretty, South Carolina was comfortably in control by halftime. A 22-2 Gamecocks run featuring 16 unanswered points, including 14 in the final 2:11 of the first half, effectively decided the game.
South Carolina's defense frustrated the Huskies most of the night, with UConn's 27% clip from the field the program's worst since at least the 1994-95 season.
Reigning national player of the yearSarah Strongfinished with 22 points but wasn't overly efficient (6-for-17 shooting) and dealt with foul trouble in a big game again.
"I think our players really lock into what we need to do on that side of the basketball," Staley said of her team's defense. "That's why we're pretty good. We got to lock in and be a little bit better on the offensive end, but our defense sets us up to have some success right now."
South Carolina senior guardTessa Johnsonestablished herself as the most dominant player on the court, finishing with a career-high 32 points. The performance came only nine days after her then-career-high 28 points against then-No. 3 USC as she continues to elevate her WNBA draft profile.
"When you're a senior, things come a lot easier," Staley said. "You see things, you know, you experience it. You know when to insert yourself. You know when to be super aggressive. ... She knew that we didn't have a 20-point scorer in the lineup, so she knew she had to take some of the brunt of missing out on Joyce."
For as lopsided as the score was at one point -- South Carolina led by as many as 17 in the third quarter -- and all of Auriemma's gripes, there were some positives for UConn, which outscored the Gamecocks in three of the four quarters by a combined 12 points and won the rebounding battle by eight. Auriemma was pleased too with the Huskies' fight after they fell behind big, cutting the deficit to as few as eight.
But their persistent inconsistency not only from game to game but within games -- which Auriemma sees as largely self-inflicted -- stuck with the coach the most.
"It's just a very, very, very immature team, basketball-wise, and maybe in general, I don't know," Auriemma said. "But to play as hard as we did, and to compete as hard as we did today, and to hurt ourselves in so many ways, it's just disappointing."
Added Strong: "I just don't think we listen to him all the time, and that we don't trust him when we need to. That's obviously on us, and we have to change."
The Huskies won't have much more time to dwell on Tuesday's result, with No. 5 Duke awaiting Saturday at Boston's TD Garden. The undefeated Gamecocks (7-0), meanwhile, next face Tennessee State on Saturday.

"It's just so out of character for anybody that's watched UConn play for 30-some years," Auriemma said of the team's issues.

South Carolina has beaten UConn in seven of the past 10 meetings, and Gamecocks coach Dawn Staley now boasts seven wins over Auriemma, tying Tara VanDerveer for second-most among nonconference opposing coaches, trailing only the late Pat Summitt (nine).
The highly anticipated top-10 showdown and Final Four rematch didn't quite live up to the hype with both programs shorthanded.
South Carolina was without top scorer and returning All-AmericanJoyce Edwardsbecause of an illness, and UConn had point guardsKK Arnold(lower body) andKayleigh Heckel(back) both sidelined.
Neither team impressed offensively, with the teams combining to shoot 29% and committing more turnovers (14 for South Carolina and 18 for UConn) than assists (10 and 8, respectively).
Even if it wasn't all pretty, South Carolina was comfortably in control by halftime.
A 22-2 Gamecocks run featuring 16 unanswered points, including 14 in the final 2:11 of the first half, effectively decided the game.
South Carolina's defense frustrated the Huskies most of the night, with UConn's 27% clip from the field the program's worst since at least the 1994-95 season.
Reigning national player of the yearSarah Strongfinished with 22 points but wasn't overly efficient (6-for-17 shooting) and dealt with foul trouble in a big game again.
"I think our players really lock into what we need to do on that side of the basketball," Staley said of her team's defense.
We got to lock in and be a little bit better on the offensive end, but our defense sets us up to have some success right now."
South Carolina senior guardTessa Johnsonestablished herself as the most dominant player on the court, finishing with a career-high 32 points.
The performance came only nine days after her then-career-high 28 points against then-No.
3 USC as she continues to elevate her WNBA draft profile.
"When you're a senior, things come a lot easier," Staley said.
She knew that we didn't have a 20-point scorer in the lineup, so she knew she had to take some of the brunt of missing out on Joyce."

For as lopsided as the score was at one point -- South Carolina led by as many as 17 in the third quarter -- and all of Auriemma's gripes, there were some positives for UConn, which outscored the Gamecocks in three of the four quarters by a combined 12 points and won the rebounding battle by eight.
Auriemma was pleased too with the Huskies' fight after they fell behind big, cutting the deficit to as few as eight.
But their persistent inconsistency not only from game to game but within games -- which Auriemma sees as largely self-inflicted -- stuck with the coach the most.
"It's just a very, very, very immature team, basketball-wise, and maybe in general, I don't know," Auriemma said.
"But to play as hard as we did, and to compete as hard as we did today, and to hurt ourselves in so many ways, it's just disappointing."
Added Strong: "I just don't think we listen to him all the time, and that we don't trust him when we need to.
That's obviously on us, and we have to change."
