Grand Theft Auto 6 is really about the death of the American Dream
The struggle is both real and virtual.
ByDevindra HardawarNov. 23, 2026 3:16 pm ESTDevindra Hardawar for EngadgetAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Even when they were well written, everyGTAstory has ultimately been about solving your problems with the accumulation of wealth. ButGrand Theft Auto 6specifically focuses on the systemic issues that make any version of the American Dream — saving money, buying a home and supporting a family with a fulfilling job — incredibly difficult for people living on the margins of society. The crushing weight of capitalism is always pressing down on you, just like in the real world.
Lucia Caminos committed an ill-conceived robbery, is subsequently sent to jail and is forced to claw her way back into civilian life with little support. Jason Duval joined the Army to escape his troubled youth and ends up serving as muscle for a small-time criminal. Much like the real Bonnie and Clyde, Lucia and Jason are driven by the need to escape poverty, but it's up to you to determine if they'll share a similar end.
I only have around 12 hours ofGTA 6under my belt so far (it's estimated to take around 50 hours to beat, and hundreds of hours to fully complete), but Rockstar clearly frames why our lead characters pursue a life of crime: beyond the generational poverty and lack of upward mobility, Lucia and Jason are also trying to build enough stability to reclaim custody of their infant son.
When she decides to stick up a payday loan store (the existence of which is inherentlypredatory against low-income people), she's doing it to feed her kid, afford diapers and survive as a single mother. (Jason isn't aware of him at that point in the story.) It's hard to imagine Lucia making such a desperate decision if she had enough social support. But of course, that's not the American way.
Six months worth of baby formula costsupwards of $2,700in the US,, whereas it's just $759 in the UK. And while America ranks fifth when it comes to the affordability of diapers changes worldwide, that's still around $1,200 a year — a significant cost for poor families. Lucia is lucky that her infant son is placed into kinship care with her aunt, instead of general foster care. Many kinship caregiversreceive foster stipends to support their charges, and fostered children also receive Medicaid for free and low-cost healthcare. Ironically, biological parentsdon't get automatic state supportfor their kids, and Medicaid eligibility depends on the family's income.
Jason has his own problems. He left the Army after unspecified "trouble" and later worked for a low-grade private security firm. Given his testy relationship to the military, he says he can't receive anyveteran home loan benefits, and that may also extend to other assistance, like employment transition and healthcare. He learns that it's easier to use the skills he's gained from the military as a tool for criminal violence, instead of following a more acceptable path like construction. He recommits to Lucia while she's in prison, andGTA 6begins with him learning that she's about to be released with close supervision. (She's getting out not because of any legal changes in her case, but because her women's prison is too full.)
Jason gets to work rebuilding a small seaside home on loan from his criminal boss (played by the great character actor Stephen Root). It's clear he can put up drywall and nail down roof tiles. But even as he prepares for a more domestic life, he's pulled deeper into the criminal underworld. It gets him some extra cash, but it also makes him a less suitable caregiver for the son he's never met.
After Jason brings Lucia home from jail, it becomes all the more clear how difficult their life is going to be.GTA 6centers heavily on their relationship (doing things like fixing up the house early on earns Lucia's favor, to theanger of online incels). But love won't be enough if they can't find a way to survive legitimately and build a safe home for their son. They can't even open a bank account, thanks to their poor credit scores. Instead, they're pushed towards a slimy Zelle/Venmo clone called BuckMe, which is specifically targeted at poor people.
It takes several hours before you can even use BuckMe or ATMs, though — until then, you're stuck hiding money under your floorboards. Jason is wise enough to start a small family fund, but it could all easily be lost if their home is robbed or destroyed (something to consider for later in the game.)GTA 6is stricter towards players when it comes to money than previous entries in the series: You lose everything you're carrying if you're killed or arrested. If you have a run-in with the cops or some baddies after a big job, it could end up being a tremendous loss.
"Everything is corrupt and rotten," Lucia says as she tries to convince Jason to hang out with her rich friends, who may be able to send more lucrative criminal work their way. "The only thing that matters is who you know and what you've got." It's a bleak point of view that might resonate with anyone who's observed the last decade of grift-driven American politics. Lucia's version of the American Dream is built on idolizing rich people living on luxury yachts and flaunting their ill-gotten wealth on social media. If society doesn't deem you worthy enough to even have a bank account, why abide by its rules?
You could try to strike it rich by robbing stores, banks and people on the street, butGTA 6's voluminous amounts of voice acting and complex character animation almost makes the prospect of random violence uncomfortably real. Sticking up a retail clerk feels bad, because you and the cashier you're aiming a gun at are both ultimately struggling to get by in an unfair country ruled by grifters. (I haven't seen the people in charge yet, but there are plenty of Trumpian parallels in the in-game right-wing TV channel Weasel.) If you try to jack the wrong car, you might get someone crashing out about how difficult their life is. Everybody hurts, even the people who seem to have it all.

Game over? How playing Grand Theft Auto VI is affecting elite athletes’ performances
Burning the midnight oil playing video games is not ideal preparation for professional sport – but it’s not all bad
“They miss games, the cheque’s still clearing. And you’re trying to tell me they got this kind of addiction to a video game that they sitting there with their thumbs looking like Donald Trump?” That was EPSN’s Stephen A Smith, one of the US’s most provocative and influential sports pundits, spitting fire and fury last week after hearing that so many NBA and NFL stars were absorbed inGrand Theft Auto VI.
Smith was hardly an outlier. Other pundits, as well as some Manchester United fans, also questioned Bryan Mbeumo’s focus and professionalism after he posted an image of GTA VI and the word “historique” after midnight on Thursday. Meanwhile before last weekend’s Premier League games, theOdd Sport social media accountpredicted that Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City would all lose. Why? Because their younger squads might be more focused on Vice City than their opponents, and therefore play with less intensity as a result. By Monday that forecast had been liked tens of thousands of times.
‘I can’t play games just for fun’: meet Javokhir Sindarov, the 20-year-old happy warrior moving for chess’s biggest prizeRead more
So is there really such a thing as a Grand Theft Auto effect, beyond all the recent hysterics and polemics? The Houston Rockets basketball player Steven Adams certainly thinks so. A couple of months ago he predicted that the launch of GTA VI would cause performances across various leagues to “plummet” in November.
Instinctively, you can see his point. If a basketball star spends hours shooting gangsters, are they really going to be as focused on shooting threes? Then again, players spend their lives around consoles. So are their levels really going to be that affected by the launch of a new game?
Fortunately the area of how video games can affect mental fatigue in elite sports stars is increasingly attracting the attention of sports scientists. And while it is still early days, the findings are certainly intriguing.
One study in 2020took 25 professional footballers in Brazil, and split them into three groups who were either made to watch adverts, play Fifa 18, or go on social media before playing a 90-minute match. The result? While the groups made a similar overall number of passes, accuracy dropped by 6.5% in the video game group compared with the control group.
Another systematic review of eight studies in 2022, which examined the link between playing video games and mental fatigue, also found that there was a “significant impact” on the technical performance of footballers – including missing more tackles and making more errors. Surprisingly, though, passing skills were unaffected.
What’s more, other studies have found that when athletes are mentally fatigued they often demonstrate longer fixation time on opponents and less on their teammates, which leads to poorer decisions. As you would also expect, mental fatigue often makes physical effort feel harder too.
However, before clubs start banning GTA VI en masse, they should hear the thoughts of John Kiely, an Irish sports scientist who recently studied mental fatigue among Brighton’s first-team players, and has also worked with Egypt’s World Cup squad in 2018, Ireland’s rugby team, and UK Athletics.
Kiely, who alsorecently co-authored a paperthat examined 28 recent academic papers on football and mental fatigue, warns there are several important caveats. Many of the studies have been conducted on small-sided training games, such as five-a-side matches between academy players. They are often small in scope. It means that what happens in the lab may not necessarily translate to the thunder and intensity of the Premier League.
View image in fullscreenManchester United’s Bryan Mbeumo posted a picture of him playing GTA VI after its launch on Thursday.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto
“The studies are way too lab-based at the moment,” he says. “And it’s very hard to extrapolate them to what will happen with a seasoned professional player who’s used to high-stress environments.”
As Kiely also points out, individual players also behave differently to the same stresses – something that he and his fellow researchers found when they monitored Brighton’s players over a season to track their mental fatigue. So playing GTA VI until 3am might affect one player a lot less than another, simply because of how their brains are wired and stimulated.
But, you might ask, surely playing esports improves reaction times and speedy decision-making? Perhaps for the general population. However, Kiely is sceptical that it transfers over to elite athletes. “The chances that the reflexes you learn on an online game are going to transfer to the field if you’re already elite are nonexistent,” he says.
However Kiely is more enthused about the potential of using eye-tracking to test a player’s reflexes when they are tired. “If you track something, be it a ball or whatever on a screen, are your left and right eyes moving simultaneously, or is there a little bit of a lag?” he asks. “Well, those lags increase with fatigue.”
So what advice would Kiely give clubs about GTA VI? Broadly they should relax – as long as players aren’t settling down for marathon sessions late at night.
“I wouldn’t see anything too much wrong with it, providing it doesn’t stimulate a player so much that they stay awake the night before a game and they lose sleep,” he says. “That’s one of the biggest dangers. Because losing sleep is a clear performance decrement and a clear injury risk promoter.
“ So my advice is play for 40 minutes, get up, take a walk, get some fresh air and do some eye exercises, and you’ll be fine.”
There is a final point worth making here. Burning the midnight oil playing a console game might not be optimal preparation for a professional player. But it certainly beats the old-school way of unwinding, of boozing and living it up out on the town.

Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop | WIREDSkip to main content
Listening to the in-gameradiostations while you cruise around inGrand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.
“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” onespotbegins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.
Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latestGTAtitle, which wasreleased after a 13-year waiton Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.
It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.
An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursdaypostedan AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic ofGTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”
Another police department in Washington state sharedGTA-likeimageryon its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” ofGTA VIby pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-seriousGTAslop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, fromEdmontontoToronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officersreactto clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.
Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks throughGTA VIfever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typicalposton the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with aGTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion,informedfollowers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”
The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success ofGTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you startfilming themduring a questionable arrest. Oneclipshowed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.
A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to theright-wing cranksupset thatGTA VIis too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.
Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tiredlaw-and-orderline onGTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t playGTAgamesbecausethey compelled you to shoot cops.
Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor ofGTAcringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.
More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its ownGTA VIrecruitment adsto blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrialGTAsludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’sdepictionof a Trumpian “golden age” withGTAgraphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted43 eligible soldiersfour days off to play the newGTAin return for reenlisting for another two years of service.
What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

I never wanted the American Dream—so I moved abroadSkip Navigation
I got my first job at 17, working the register at an Eckerd's drugstore in Texas. My manager was only a few years older than me, and while my coworkers seemed motivated by the idea of working their way up to his position, I felt no desire to follow that path.
It all felt suffocating: the added responsibility, the longer hours, the idea that this was the ladder I was supposed to want to climb. I wanted to work, but I couldn't wrap my head around building my whole identity around a job.
I never wantedthe American DreamI saw so many people around me striving to achieve. For a long time, I wondered if something was wrong with me. It wasn't until I finally made a long-term move abroad about a decade ago that I realized it was okay to want something different.
I never dreamed about traditional milestones
After college, I got a job in travel sales. I was good at it. Talking about travel all day suited the wanderlust I'd carried since my first trip abroad in my teens.
I continued working in sales, marketing and the odd temp role for years. But they were always just jobs. I didn't feel like they defined me or feel a calling to an industry or title the way people around me seemed to.
Of course, I wanted financial stability, but I was unwilling to sacrifice my time and well-being to get it. I just didn't connect with the version of ambition that meant grinding toward a corner office. What I wanted the most wasn't status; it was freedom, growth and new experiences.
In Madrid, Spain.Courtesy of Cepee Tabibian
The wanderlust eventually caught up to me, and at 26 I moved to Spain to teach English. Even though I was working, people saw it as taking a year off from my career and warned me it could damage my resume. I simply didn't care. Living for my resume had never made sense to me.
Looking back, I think being abroad offered an escape from the pressure to chase the traditional path of the American Dream. There, I felt free to enjoy life and figure out who I was without worrying about what box I needed to tick next.
I wanted to stay in Spain, but I couldn't find a visa that would let melive therelong-term, so I returned to the U.S. I became a serial job hopper for almost 10 years,quitting a jobevery year to spend summers visiting friends in the Netherlands, the U.K. and Switzerland or solo traveling in Spain on the money I'd saved up.
In Granada, Spain.Courtesy of Cepee Tabibian
On the personal side, I wasn't in a rush to get married orhave kids. In my 30s, single and childfree, I felt like I was failing at adulthood, even though deep down, I didn't actually want the things I was supposedly behind on. Settling down just because everyone else was doing it never felt right to me.
And I couldn't shake the dream of living in Europe. In my 20s, people mostly assumed my desire to travel was a phase. By my 30s, the conversations had shifted and I was getting pulled aside. Friends, family and colleagues all had some version of the same message: It was time to get serious and build a life in Texas.
But my gut said to try one more time. So I did.
Moving abroad helped me redefine success
In 2015, on my fourth attempt, I finallymade it to Spain for good. It was scary to shake things up when everyone around me was settling down, but deep down I knew at 35, this was my chance to stop trying to conform and start building a life that felt right for me.
In my new home, the pace was slower. I quickly noticed that people actually took their vacations. Strangers at a dinner party didn't immediately ask me what I did for work. Adults in their 30s, 40s and beyond were out living full social lives. Single, childfree women my age didn't feel like an anomaly.
Living abroad didn't solve everything overnight. I still had to figure out how to support myself. But having the space to define myself professionally without constant judgment changed what felt possible.
In Cádiz, Spain.Courtesy of Cepee Tabibian
In 2017, I launchedShe Hit Refresh, where I help women over 30 figure out how to move to Europe and build new lives for themselves. It's not something I could have created from anywhere else, with any other experience than my own.
In the process, I've met so many others who left corporate America behind to create something different for themselves. I've seen more women asking the same questions I spent years asking myself. Burnt out, disillusioned with hustle culture, realizing that checking all the boxes of the American Dream they grew up on didn't deliver the feeling they were promised.
We're all figuring it out together; each of us writing a version of a life that didn't fit a standard template. Moving abroad helped me understand that success, for me, was never about earning more or owning more. It was always about more ease, more time, more space, more life.
For years, I thought I was behind. I felt like something was wrong with me for wanting a different kind of life. Looking back, I just hadn't found my place yet.
Cepee Tabibianis the founder ofShe Hit Refresh, where she's helped over 24,000 women age 30+ plan their move abroad. Grab her freeMove Abroad After 30 Guideto start planning your own move. The daughter of Colombian and Iranian immigrants, Cepee grew up in Houston, Texas, before becoming an immigrant herself in Spain. Follow her@shehitrefresh.

Turkish police hunting for lioness stalking Istanbul | News | Al Jazeera

Add Al Jazeera on GoogleResidents have been warned of the danger, and police have been stationed on roads leading into and out of Zekeriyakoy, the neighbourhood north of Istanbul where surveillance cameras have spotted the lion [File: Reuters]ByAFPandAPPublished On 23 Nov 202623 Nov 2026
Police and animal welfare teams have launched a hunt for a lioness reported to be prowling the outskirts of Istanbul.
City authorities closed a woodland area in the northern Sariyer district on Monday as the teams expanded a search for the big cat, which was spotted in the area the previous evening.

list 2 of 3Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
list 3 of 3A geography of hearts: Turkiye and Lebanon, building the Levant together
Turkiye’s National Parks Directorate said on Sunday that police officers in Zekeriyakoy, north of Istanbul’s European side, had reported spotting “an animal resembling a lion” on surveillance cameras.
Grainy security camera footage republished by Turkish media appeared to show what looked like a big cat prowling across a patch of open countryside.
Istanbul Governor Davut Gul’s office confirmed the information, saying that “the necessary care is being taken to capture it alive”.
The parks authority said specialist veterinarians and teams equipped with thermal imaging cameras were assisting in the search.
More than 70 personnel, supported by drones, were searching in and around the nearby Belgrade Forest, which covers 54 square kilometres (21 square miles) north of Istanbul.
Local resident Arda Koc said he saw the lioness after joining the search on Sunday evening.
“I took my car and went out for a drive hoping to see it,” he told Turkiye’s Cumhuriyet newspaper. “While I was driving, it suddenly jumped out in front of me. At first I was scared. After that, I immediately notified the gendarmerie.”
Residents have been warned of the danger, and police were stationed on roads leading into and out of the neighbourhood.
Sariyer District Mayor Mustafa Oktay Aksu noted that the lioness had not harmed chickens she passed at night, indicating she had been hand-reared. However, he warned that she should still be treated as dangerous.
Meanwhile, activists and professors have questioned how the species was brought into Turkiye.
Doganay Tolunay, a professor in the forestry department of Istanbul University-Cerrahpasa,saidon X on Monday that questions that need to be asked should include “how a globally threatened species was brought into our country, how it got through customs, why those feeding it have yet to be identified” and “what will happen if the lion is caught”.
Turkiye has become a hub for the illegal trade in wild animals as traffickers exploit its air links to Africa and Asia.
In December 2024, a young gorilla was rescued after being discovered at Istanbul Airport on a flight from Nigeria to Thailand.

Turkish authorities search for lion spotted on outskirts of Istanbul | Euronews
ByBurcu Basaran&Gavin BlackburnPublished on23 November 2026 - 8:48 GMT+1ShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
The National Parks Directorate said specialist veterinarians and teams equipped with thermal imaging cameras were assisting the search, which was focused on a wooded area.
Police and animal welfare teams in Istanbul are searching for a female lion seen prowling the city’s outskirts, Turkish officials said on Monday.
A resident in the Uskumruköy neighborhood spotted the animal on Sunday evening, and it was later seen on security camera footage.
Uskumruköy is on the northern edge of Istanbul’s European side, an area surrounded by forests.
“The location of the lion has been identified and the necessary care is being taken to capture it alive,” the Istanbul governor’s office said in a statement posted on social media.
Grainy images published by the DHA news agency showed the lion walking through a grassy area.
It was unclear where the lion came from, but some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home.
Local residents have been warned of the dangers.
Sarıyer Mayor Mustafa Oktay Aksu warned local residents to take precautions, saying: "We kindly ask residents not to leave their homes, both so that they are not harmed and so that they do not hinder the operation."
Aksu said it was not yet known where the lion had come from, and that they were considering the possibility that it may have been raised by a private individual.
Uskumruköy neighbourhood head Şeyda Üst also said in a statement that she had been living in the area for about 22 years, that she had previously dealt with reports of monkeys and snakes, but that this was the first time a lion had been seen.
Üst said teams were continuing their work in the area, that the lion had been detected using heat-sensitive drones, that the necessary warnings had been issued to residents and that they were waiting for the animal to be captured.
In Turkey, individuals are not allowed to keep aggressive and predatory wild animals such as lions as a hobby or as pets. Housing such animals is subject to regulations for facilities licensed under the relevant legislation, such as zoos and wildlife parks.

Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as its tankers get ready to break the US blockade | Euronews
ByPeter Barabas&Euronews Doha bureauPublished on21 November 2026 - 22:32 GMT+1,Updated23:54ShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
The “no war, no peace” US-Iran confrontation appears to be moving towards a possible breaking point as Iran increases its military actions in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while its critical attempt to break the US military naval blockade in the Persian Gulf appears to be imminent.
Iran launched two waves of drone and ballistic missile attacks on Saturday night against four US bases in Bahrain, home to the US’ Fifth Fleet headquarters, the Iranian media reported, while Bahrain announced the attacks, warning the population to shelter.
Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency claimed that the Iranian military targeted four US bases in Bahrain, with two of the named as Sheikh Isa and Juffair, in what it called a response to continued US incursions in Iran’s airspace.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed that it struck 2 Patriot defence batteries and a radar system. Bahrain and the US military did not confirm the claims.
Bahrain said that its air defence intercepted several Iranian attacks, calling them a “heinous Iranian aggression”.
Local sources in Bahrain reported loud explosions and Bahrain’s Interior ministry announced that a fire broke out at a civilian industrial compound, with no injuries reported, while local videos showed smoke rising from a fire in an unidentified location.
Right after the attack on Bahrain, reports emerged from southern Iran of explosions in Sirik. The US military has retaliated regularly against Iranian military facilities in recent weeks.
Earlier on Saturday, US Central Command CENTCOM denied Iranian claims that a surface-to-air missile damaged a US F-16 fighter jet on Friday evening.
Meanwhile, at least three oil tankers were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in what appeared to be the latest Iranian strikes on shipping through the strategic chokepoint.
In a sharp increase of incidents in the Strait of Hormuz over the last week, the UK military’s maritime security center (UKMTO) said two tankers were struck separately by projectiles early Saturday while exiting the Persian Gulf through the strait. There were no reports of casualties.
The Iranian navy said in a statement carried on state media that a tanker hit a naval mine east of the strait and caught fire. State media also said that the military carried out its most “intense and varied” operations yet in the strait overnight to stop vessels.
Iran’s army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia warned the US again on Saturday that any attack on Iran will be met with “a decisive and immediate response” as “we are much stronger than in the past,” Iranian TV IRIB report.
“Any new aggression will be met with a decisive, immediate and effective response from the armed forces, and the defence of the country will not be limited to a specific geographical area,” Akraminia said during a visit to Iranian troops in the south of the country.
The Iranian TV showed for the first time the ground troops deployed into defensive positions in the coastal areas of southern Iran on Saturday.
Meanwhile on Saturday, as more than 14 Iranian tankers are reported to be prepared off Kharg Island to break out of the US military blockade in the coming days, Iran’s deputy minister of foreign affairs Kazem Gharibabadi told Iranian media that the US blockade of Iranian ports “is an act of war and we will take any necessary measures to break this economic siege.”
Iran warned of a “fierce military response” if the convoy was engaged by the US military, threatening with widespread attacks on energy infrastructures across the Gulf region.
Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian also said that Iran is subject to a “silent economic war” which is “tougher than a war with missiles,” adding that Iran has the capability to withstand it.
As Gharibabadi announced that Tehran has warned the United States that the Iranian convoy will sail soon to China, the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War said that “Iranian attempts to run the blockade impose a series of dilemmas on the United States by either collapsing the blockade or returning to a war that imposes unideal political costs on the United States by straining its relationships with Gulf allies.”
Against the backdrop of the intensifying crisis, the diplomatic negotiations between the US and Iran spearheaded by Qatar continue.
Iran’s deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi announced on Saturday that a Qatari delegation held talks with Iranian officials on Friday evening for some two hours, before returning to Doha.
Iranian Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi suggested that a deal is possible when he declared that reopening the Strait of Hormuz would be “not difficult” if the US accepted Iran’s “reasonable conditions,” especially by ending the blockade which he called “completely illegal,” lifting sanctions and Washington acknowledging “past mistakes.”
In parallel, US president Donald Trump told US network Fox News on Saturday that he planned to make a “permanent” deal with Iran to prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon and that he was never interested in a regime change in Iran.
“I intend to reach a permanent deal with Iran that prevents them from obtaining nuclear weapons, even if another president takes my place in the future and is unfit for the office,” Trump said.

lead_title: Washington Spirit part ways with Adrian Gonzalez after loss in NWSL Championship

evidence_pages.https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/wa:
Washington Spirit part ways with Adrian Gonzalez after loss in NWSL Championship - CBS Sportssite: media | arena: soccer | pageType: stories | section: | slug: washington-spirit-adrian-gonzalez-nwsl-championship | sport: soccer | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/soccer/reg/free/storiesSkip to Main Content
Washington Spirit part ways with Adrian Gonzalez after loss in NWSL Championship
Gonzalez was at the helm for both Saturday's defeat to the Kansas City Current and the 2025 loss in the NWSL Championship to Gotham FC
ByPardeep CattryNov 23, 2026at 3:34 pm ET•4 min readGetty Images
The Washington Spirit parted ways with head coach Adrian Gonzalez on Monday, less than 48 hours after a2-1 lossto the Kansas City Current that marked the team's third successive defeat in the NWSL Championship.
Gonzalez was an assistant on the 2024 team that lost to the Orlando Pride in the final but he served as the interim before Jonatan Giraldez's midseason arrival from Barcelona. He then succeeded Giraldez after he left for France's OL Lyonnes, another club in Spirit owner Michele Kang's portfolio, midway through the 2025 campaign. He was a finalist for the NWSL's coach of the year award last season and maintained a consistency that has been a trademark for the Spirit in recent years, ensuring they continued to be serial contenders for titles under both Giraldez and Gonzalez.
For all their ambition, though, the Spirit have struggled to win major titles in the years since Kang took over the club in 2022. Their only title since is the 2025 Challenge Cup, a one-off game against the Pride, and have failed to win the NWSL Shield despite inching close on a handful of occasions while also falling short in the NWSL Championship games. They also failed to win the Concacaf W Champions Cup earlier this year, losing 5-3 to Club America in the final.
"I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," Gonzalez said in a club statement. "It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown. A special thank you to the Spirit fans, who make this club truly unique. The connection and bond we've built with you has meant so much to me and made my time here even more special. Your passion and support are something I will always remember. While this chapter comes to an end, I'm excited for what lies ahead for the club and wish everyone continued success."
Gonzalez's departure also comes after Haley Carter became the president of soccer operations in the build-up to the 2026 season. Carter was previously with the Orlando Pride, who won both the NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship in 2024 after years of being a bottom-dweller in the league.
"We are grateful to Adrian for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Carter said in a statement. "He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club. As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."
The search for Gonzalez's successor is underway and is likely to center around the Spirit's continuing quest to win the NWSL's top titles.
Spirit's title chase dictates coaching change
Since Kang's 2022 takeover, the ambitions of the Spirit have been clear as day. This is a team that is purpose-built to compete for titles, to the point that their attempts to keep Trinity Rodman in the NWSLled the league to create a brand-new ruleand ahistoric contract for the player herself. The Spirit's entire roster, though, is impressive in its own right – Rodman counts Italy international Sofia Cantore amongst her partners in attack, while Tanzania's Clare Luvanga has scored four goals and notched three assists since her September arrival.
Gonzalez understood the assignment, even if the only accolade he walked away with was the 2025 Challenge Cup. Washington, DC –Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.
For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.

This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.
The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.
The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.
And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.
“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.
After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.
“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.
“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”
That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.
Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.
The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”
For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.
The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.
The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.
Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.
“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.
“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”
A bus in Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, says ‘Go Spirit!’ ahead of the NWSL final, November 21 [Ali Harb/Al Jazeera]
KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.
Rodman scored from a header minutes later.
The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.
Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.
Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.
“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.
“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”
Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.
And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.
The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.
Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.
On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.

Washington Spirit part ways with Adrian Gonzalez after loss in NWSL Championship
Gonzalez was at the helm for both Saturday's defeat to the Kansas City Current and the 2025 loss in the NWSL Championship to Gotham FC
ByPardeep CattryNov 23, 2026at 3:34 pm ET•4 min readGetty Images

The Washington Spirit parted ways with head coach Adrian Gonzalez on Monday, less than 48 hours after a2-1 lossto the Kansas City Current that marked the team's third successive defeat in the NWSL Championship.
Gonzalez was an assistant on the 2024 team that lost to the Orlando Pride in the final but he served as the interim before Jonatan Giraldez's midseason arrival from Barcelona.
He then succeeded Giraldez after he left for France's OL Lyonnes, another club in Spirit owner Michele Kang's portfolio, midway through the 2025 campaign.

He was a finalist for the NWSL's coach of the year award last season and maintained a consistency that has been a trademark for the Spirit in recent years, ensuring they continued to be serial contenders for titles under both Giraldez and Gonzalez.
For all their ambition, though, the Spirit have struggled to win major titles in the years since Kang took over the club in 2022.

Their only title since is the 2025 Challenge Cup, a one-off game against the Pride, and have failed to win the NWSL Shield despite inching close on a handful of occasions while also falling short in the NWSL Championship games.
They also failed to win the Concacaf W Champions Cup earlier this year, losing 5-3 to Club America in the final.

"I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," Gonzalez said in a club statement.
"It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown.
A special thank you to the Spirit fans, who make this club truly unique.
The connection and bond we've built with you has meant so much to me and made my time here even more special.
Your passion and support are something I will always remember.
While this chapter comes to an end, I'm excited for what lies ahead for the club and wish everyone continued success."
Gonzalez's departure also comes after Haley Carter became the president of soccer operations in the build-up to the 2026 season.
Carter was previously with the Orlando Pride, who won both the NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship in 2024 after years of being a bottom-dweller in the league.
"We are grateful to Adrian for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Carter said in a statement.
"He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club.
As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."
The search for Gonzalez's successor is underway and is likely to center around the Spirit's continuing quest to win the NWSL's top titles.
Since Kang's 2022 takeover, the ambitions of the Spirit have been clear as day.

This is a team that is purpose-built to compete for titles, to the point that their attempts to keep Trinity Rodman in the NWSLled the league to create a brand-new ruleand ahistoric contract for the player herself.

The Spirit's entire roster, though, is impressive in its own right – Rodman counts Italy international Sofia Cantore amongst her partners in attack, while Tanzania's Clare Luvanga has scored four goals and notched three assists since her September arrival.
Gonzalez understood the assignment, even if the only accolade he walked away with was the 2025 Challenge Cup.
He actually leaves the Spirit with 32 wins from 58 and a1.84 points-per-game record, the best tally from a coach in the history of the NWSL.

The strike on his record is that the Spirit did not rise to the occasion in the championship both last year and especially on Saturday, when a physical Current disrupted the momentum of the game and rattled the Spirit from start to finish.

His will be a tough act to follow, though – he was able to get the best out of the players despite the stop-start nature of his responsibilities in the early stretch of his tenure and only confirmed that the Spirit are a club with high standards.
Considering the ambitions of the club, the coaching search will be an intriguing one.

The Spirit are an attack-minded team and it would not be a surprise if a coach of that ilk lands the job, but Gonzalez's successor will ultimately be tasked with actually winning the titles that have eluded the club in recent years.
Someone with a winning track record might be preferred and even if there are few obvious candidates, the Spirit likely have the pull – and the resources – to sign almost anyone they would like.

It is not the only layer of uncertainty as the search begins – Carter has never hired a head coach during her years in NWSL front offices, joining the Pride after Seb Hines took the role and departing before his August departure.

article.title: Các quan chức lên án vụ bắt giữ của ICE tại sân bay Seattle
article.summary: Các quan chức đã lên án vụ bắt giữ của Cơ quan Di trú và Hải quan Hoa Kỳ (ICE) tại sân bay Seattle, mô tả hành động này là 'kinh hoàng' và 'làm lạnh máu'.
body: Các quan chức đã lên án vụ bắt giữ của Cơ quan Di trú và Hải quan Hoa Kỳ (ICE) tại sân bay Seattle, mô tả hành động này là 'kinh hoàng' và 'làm lạnh máu'. Vụ bắt giữ diễn ra vào sáng thứ Bảy tại sân bay quốc tế Seattle-Tacoma, khi hành khách đang lên máy bay đi Los Angeles.

Thống đốc bang Washington, Bob Ferguson, đã gọi ICE là 'hoàn toàn và tuyệt đối mất kiểm soát' và mô tả video về vụ bắt giữ là 'kinh hoàng' và 'làm lạnh máu'. Ông cũng đặt câu hỏi về việc liệu các đặc vụ có vi phạm luật của bang Washington, mà ông đã ký vào tháng 3, cấm các sĩ quan thực thi pháp luật mặc mặt nạ.
Các quan chức khác, bao gồm Thị trưởng Seattle Katie Wilson, cũng đã lên án vụ bắt giữ, mô tả hành động của các đặc vụ là 'không thể chấp nhận được và không phải là người Mỹ'.
Vụ bắt giữ đã gây ra sự phản đối từ công chúng, với nhiều người biểu tình tập trung tại sân bay vào chiều thứ Bảy để lên án vụ bắt giữ và yêu cầu trách nhiệm từ các cơ quan liên bang.

article.title: Tàu chiến Nga bị tấn công chìm tại căn cứ hải quân Libya
article.summary: Tổng thống Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy xác nhận quân đội nước này đứng sau vụ tập kích bằng xuồng không người lái nhằm vào tàu chiến và tàu hàng của Nga ngoài khơi Libya.
body: Vụ tấn công xảy ra vào chủ nhật tại căn cứ hải quân Benghazi ở miền đông Libya, khiến tàu hộ vệ Merkury của Hải quân Nga hứng chịu hư hại nặng nề, bốc cháy và sau đó chìm một phần. Hình ảnh vệ tinh và thông tin từ các quan chức địa phương xác nhận vụ việc diễn ra khi chiến hạm này ghé cảng để tiếp tế nhiên liệu theo thỏa thuận hợp tác giữa Nga và chính quyền miền đông Libya.

Đến ngày thứ hai, Tổng thống Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy chính thức xác nhận lực lượng vũ trang nước này đã tiến hành các cuộc tập kích bằng xuồng không người lái trên vùng biển Libya. Ngoài tàu hộ vệ Merkury, phía Ukraine còn cho biết đã nhắm mục tiêu vào tàu chở hàng khô MV Angara được cho là dùng để vận chuyển vũ khí, trong chiến dịch nhằm vào các tài sản hải quân và đội tàu ngầm của Nga.

Sự việc lập tức dấy lên lo ngại quốc tế về nguy cơ xung đột Nga - Ukraine lan rộng sang khu vực Bắc Phi. Chính quyền miền đông Libya thông báo đã khởi động một cuộc điều tra chung với Nga để làm rõ nguyên nhân, đồng thời lên án hành vi biến lãnh thổ và cảng biển nước này thành nơi giải quyết mâu thuẫn quốc tế. Trong khi đó, chính quyền miền tây Libya và Phái bộ Hỗ trợ của Liên hợp quốc tại Libya (UNSMIL) cũng bày tỏ quan ngại sâu sắc, kêu gọi mở một cuộc điều tra độc lập và minh bạch.

Phía Kremlin chỉ trích các cuộc tấn công này là xu hướng rất nguy hiểm và cảnh báo sẽ có biện pháp đáp trả. Sự việc tại Benghazi phản ánh rõ nét những rủi ro khi các cơ sở hạ tầng dân sự và cảng biển tại một quốc gia vẫn đang chia rẽ chính trị như Libya bị kéo vào vòng xoáy của các cuộc đối đầu ngoại giao và quân sự giữa các cường quốc bên ngoài.

article.title: Huấn luyện viên Diego Simeone phá kỷ lục La Liga
article.summary: Huấn luyện viên Diego Simeone của Atletico Madrid đã phá kỷ lục La Liga với 345 trận thắng
body: Huấn luyện viên Diego Simeone của Atletico Madrid đã phá kỷ lục La Liga với 345 trận thắng. Ông đã vượt qua kỷ lục của huấn luyện viên Luis Aragones, người đã giành 344 trận thắng trong sự nghiệp của mình.

Simeone đã đạt được thành tích này sau khi Atletico Madrid giành chiến thắng 3-0 trước Getafe. Chiến thắng này đã giúp Atletico Madrid đứng thứ 3 trên bảng xếp hạng sau 10 trận thắng trong 13 trận đấu.

Simeone đã phản hồi về việc bị coi là một huấn luyện viên phòng ngự, ông cho rằng: "Bạn không thể thắng 345 trận chỉ bằng cách phòng ngự." Ông cũng cho biết rằng có một lượng công việc khổng lồ đằng sau thành tích này.

lead_title: ‘Horrific’ and ‘chilling’: Officials condemn ICE arrests at Seattle airport

evidence_pages.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2:
‘Horrific’ and ‘chilling’: Officials condemn ICE arrests at Seattle airport | Migration News | Al Jazeera
Share ‘Horrific’ and ‘chilling’: Officials condemn ICE arrests at Seattle airport on social media
Add Al Jazeera on GoogleThe arrests at the Seattle-Tacoma international airport prompted protests on Saturday night [File: Lindsey Wasson/AP]ByCatherine NouhanPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026
Democrats and state officials have denounced a now-viral immigration arrest in Washington state, which took place on an airport jet bridge as passengers were boarding a flight to Los Angeles.
“What we’ve seen happening in Washington is atrocious,” said Nevada’s Governor-elect Aaron Ford, a Democrat, in an interview with the news outlet MS NOW on Sunday.

list 2 of 3Surging ICE raids shadow final weeks of California congressional race
list 3 of 3Venezuelan boxer Linares arrested in US and faces deportation, ICE confirms
He added that he supported safeguards to restrict the actions taken by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.
“ We need some control over these vigilante ICE agents who come en masse in terrorising neighbourhoods, at airports included,” Ford said.
The two arrests unfolded on Saturday morning at Seattle-Tacoma international airport, as passengers boarded Alaska Airlines Flight 1306.
Videos recorded by passengers showed immigration agents in masks surrounding a man and a woman on the narrow jet bridge, forcing them to the ground as other travellers looked on.
Passengers could be heard asking the officers to identify themselves, while a woman repeatedly shouted that she and her family had work permits.
In one video, a young girl can be heard screaming as officers remove a man through a side door. In another part of the footage, an officer appeared to shove a bystander who tried to intervene.
The flight was delayed, eventually departing about three hours later than expected.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) defended the operation, saying ICE had conducted a targeted enforcement action to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who the agency said had overstayed his visa.
DHS alleged that other travellers began obstructing and assaulting officers during the arrest, including one passenger who allegedly “hurled hot coffee on the officers”.
The woman who was arrested, identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, was also found to have overstayed her visa, the department said, adding that she would be charged with assaulting a federal officer.
The agency did not say where the two were taken.
The footage prompted sharp condemnation from Washington Governor Bob Ferguson, who called ICE “completely and totally out of control” and described the video as “horrific” and “chilling” at a news conference on Saturday.
Ferguson also questioned whether the agents violated a Washington state law he signed in March that restricts law enforcement officers from wearing facial coverings.
“Masked agents who do not identify themselves drag screaming individuals off a jetway as they’re about to do something very ordinary in our country: board a flight. There is no justification for this brutality,” Ferguson said during the news conference.
He added that state officials were investigating the circumstances of the arrests, including how the agents accessed the jet bridge.
Ferguson also urged Alaska Airlines and other carriers to demand that federal immigration agents leave airports.
Alaska Airlines said it did not receive advance notice of the enforcement operation and was working with Ferguson and the Port of Seattle to determine whether established protocols had been followed.
The Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, said in a statement that it has raised its concerns with the relevant federal authorities about whether regulations were breached.
At Saturday’s news conference, Port of Seattle Commissioner Hamdi Mohamed characterised the arrests as particularly distressing because of when they took place.
“We are entering the holidays. That is one of the most heartbreaking things about this moment today. There are so many people in that airport that are travelling to go and connect with their families,” Mohamed said. “And that family is separated.”
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson also condemned the operation, describing the agents’ tactics as “unacceptable and un-American”.
Protesters gathered at the airport on Saturday evening, in the hours after the confrontation, to condemn the arrests and call for accountability from federal authorities.
A protester argues with a police officer during a demonstration at the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on November 21, 2026 [David Ryder/Reuters]
Disapproval of Trump’s immigration crackdown
The arrests come as President Donald Trump continues to pursue what he has promised will be the largest deportation effort in US history.
But voters have expressed concern about the tactics used during his immigration crackdown. Some experts believe the topic became apolitical liability for Republicansin the November 3 midterm elections.
A Fox News poll from September found that 53 percent of registered voters believed the administration’simmigration enforcement had gone too far. The figure rose to 60 percent among independent voters and two-thirds of Hispanic respondents.
In a November 8 interview with the CBS News television programme 60 Minutes, Trump acknowledged that his administration’s deportation policies may have been too aggressive, saying, “I think it might be too tough, yeah.”
In the midterms, the Democratic Party won majorities in both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, flipping both chambers from Republican control.
In the wake of that victory, several high-profile members of the left-wing party have pledged to seek reforms to immigration enforcement operations in the US.
Senators Alex Padilla and Jacky Rosen, for instance, have introduced legislation that would prevent ICE from carrying out arrests at or near airports without a judicial warrant first.
Patty Murray, another Democratic senator, also said she was demanding answers from DHS and warned in a post on X that the administration would face consequences when theincoming Congressis sworn in early next year.
“Trump answers to a Democratic Congress on January 3rd – there WILL be accountability,” she wrote.

lead_title: Russian warship hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say

evidence_pages.https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261:
Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say - France 24Skip to main content
Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.
Issued on:22/11/2026 - 20:41Modified:23/11/2026 - 09:00
3 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24Video by:Simon MORITZ
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Try againCover image: Capsized Russian navy corvette Merkury is seen following a suspected drone strike, at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya, November 22, 2026. © AP via Vanto satellite image01:27
AUkrainiandrone strike hit a Russian warship Sunday at a naval base inLibya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war. A commercial vessel off the port was also hit.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that Ukraine's military had carried out the attacks using naval drones.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press.
They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
Try againCover image: © France 2405:03
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictatorMuammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based inTripoliand a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
Read moreRussia turns to Libyan ports after Assad's ouster in Syria
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Sunday caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.
The vessel had docked at the base for refueling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement betweenRussiaand the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.
A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.
On Sunday evening, local media said that another sea drone hit a commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack.
Local officials said a "merchant vessel was targeted this evening by explosive-laden sea drones off the coast of Benghazi", but did not specify whether the ship had been Russian as well.
Reports said the second ship was sailing under a Maltese flag.
The eastern Libyan administration said all crew members had been rescued and were receiving treatment for minor injuries.
Libya Alhadath television later reported that naval and air force units intercepted more than 12 "explosive-laden sea drones" off Benghazi.
No further details were given. The Almasar satellite television channel said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.
'Dragging' Libyan ports 'into external conflicts'
The western Libya government expressed concerns about “dragging Libyan ports and civilian facilities into external conflicts,” in an apparent reference to the war in Ukraine.
“The government reaffirms its categorical rejection of turning Libya into an arena for international conflicts or a theater for external powers to settle scores,” it said in a statement.
In March, Ukrainian forces operating in western Libya under a covert deal struck a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in a suspected sea drone attack near Maltese waters, Libyan officials said at the time.
The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, operated mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also at other military facilities in the capital, Tripoli, and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press.
The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".
"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X.

Ukraine has claimed responsibility for sinking a Russian warship and striking a cargo vessel off Libya’s coast, raising concerns about the Russia-Ukraine war widening geographically.
“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a post on X on Monday.

list 2 of 3Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
list 3 of 3Crew evacuated amid battle to put out fire on Russian ship hit by drones
The attack targeted the Russian corvette Merkury and the cargo vessel MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said was used to transport weapons.
The attacks come amid an intensifying Ukrainian campaign targeting Russian naval assets, energy infrastructure and vessels linked to Moscow’s so-called shadow fleet, which helps Russia circumvent Western sanctions.
The developments have also raised questions about the involvement of foreign powers in a divided Libya, and the risk of drawing other nations into the conflict, nearly five years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Here is what we know about the attacks, who may be behind them and what they mean for the expanding reach of the war.
The Russian Navy’s Merkury was struck at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya on Sunday, triggering an explosion and fire.
Satellite imagery showed most of the corvette had capsized and sunk, with only its bow visible above water.
Zelenskyy confirmed the sinking on Monday, saying a Russian Kamov Ka-27 military helicopter was also destroyed.
“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added.
A day earlier, the Russian cargo ship Sparta II was struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland. The vessel caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters. All 16 crew members were evacuated, with one slightly injured.
In Finland, the military assessed the vessel was likely struck by Ukraine. Russian authorities said two drones hit the Sparta II in international waters. Kyiv has not publicly claimed responsibility for Sunday’s attack.
Zelenskyy said his country would continue to launch operations in designated maritime areas in response to Russia’s aggression.
Kyiv’s attacks come as Russia has intensified its air attacks across Ukraine, using ballistic missiles, drones and guided bombs. Energy facilities, bridges, Black Sea ports and other civilian infrastructure have been targeted in Ukraine, which has countered with attacks on Russian energy sites and other targets.

Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say

A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

© AP via Vanto satellite image01:27
AUkrainiandrone strike hit a Russian warship Sunday at a naval base inLibya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
A commercial vessel off the port was also hit.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that Ukraine's military had carried out the attacks using naval drones.

The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press.
They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack.
At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
Try againCover image: © France 2405:03

The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictatorMuammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011.
A UN-supported government is based inTripoliand a rival administration is located in the east.
The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
Read moreRussia turns to Libyan ports after Assad's ouster in Syria
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Sunday caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.

The vessel had docked at the base for refueling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement betweenRussiaand the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.
A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.
On Sunday evening, local media said that another sea drone hit a commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack.
Local officials said a "merchant vessel was targeted this evening by explosive-laden sea drones off the coast of Benghazi", but did not specify whether the ship had been Russian as well.
Reports said the second ship was sailing under a Maltese flag.
The eastern Libyan administration said all crew members had been rescued and were receiving treatment for minor injuries.
Libya Alhadath television later reported that naval and air force units intercepted more than 12 "explosive-laden sea drones" off Benghazi.
The Almasar satellite television channel said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.
The western Libya government expressed concerns about “dragging Libyan ports and civilian facilities into external conflicts,” in an apparent reference to the war in Ukraine.
“The government reaffirms its categorical rejection of turning Libya into an arena for international conflicts or a theater for external powers to settle scores,” it said in a statement.

In March, Ukrainian forces operating in western Libya under a covert deal struck a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in a suspected sea drone attack near Maltese waters, Libyan officials said at the time.

The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, operated mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also at other military facilities in the capital, Tripoli, and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press.
The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".
"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X.

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Diego Simeone: Atletico Madrid boss breaks La Liga victories record - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Diego Simeone beat the record of Luis Aragones, who recorded his final La Liga victory in 2004
Published23 November 2026, 10:48 GMT
Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club.
Sunday'striumph at Estadio Coliseumwas the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight.
Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total.
"It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games.
"I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this."
Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face".
He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it.
"This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?"
The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain.
He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure.
Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later.
He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign.
Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge.
However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016.
Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018.
His contract expires at theend of this seasonwith the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign.
ByGuillem BalagueBBC Sport Columnist
There has been an evolution since Simeone arrived, but his peak came when his players were happy to defend without the ball, deep in their own box. That is how the titles arrived.
He has not found the same effort or quality with a squad built to attack. In the peak years he found the perfect balance between deep defence and counterattack, yet picking it is harder now that his team must take the initiative.
None of that diminishes his legacy. He turned the club's mentality into a winning one and sustained it for over a decade, the two hardest things in football.
After losing a second Champions League final to Real Madrid in 2016 he could have left, but he renewed his energy.
Atletico have flirted with Luis Enrique and Unai Emery, yet everyone agrees he goes when he decides. For now, he finds plenty of reasons to stay.
